Title: Haze: Outdoor events may be moved indoors as 808 hotspots detected in Kalimantan
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Organisers may need to move outdoor events indoors if air quality deteriorates amid the current haze situation, said Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup.
He said the move was important to reduce public exposure to polluted air, particularly when Air Pollutant Index (API) readings reached unhealthy levels.
He said appropriate measures would be taken based on prevailing haze conditions and API readings, in line with the Haze Action Plan and standard operating procedures.
"For example, the Malaysia Day celebration in Kuching was moved indoors to the Borneo Convention Centre, while fireworks were not allowed.
"We will therefore monitor the situation and adjust outdoor events according to the haze conditions," he said.
Arthur was speaking to reporters after the Leadership Session held in conjunction with the 2026/2027 Orientation Week at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) Chancellor's Hall here yesterday.
He said conditions remained under control when API readings were in the green or blue categories, classified as good and moderate, respectively.
However, an unhealthy yellow reading would trigger warnings and increased coordination with relevant agencies and ministries.
"If it reaches the red or very unhealthy level, more drastic measures can be taken, including declaring a local emergency, as happened previously in Serian and Kuching before conditions improved," he said.
On the haze situation in Kalimantan, Arthur said Malaysia's offer of assistance to Indonesia to combat forest fires remained available, including aircraft for water-bombing operations and personnel.
He said he had discussed the increase in hotspots in Kalimantan with Indonesia's Environment Minister through face-to-face meetings and phone calls.
"Haze is a transboundary issue, and what happens in one country will affect neighbouring countries," he said.

Title: Bersatu Perlis hit by mass resignations, 114 branch chiefs quit
Article:
ARAU: The resignation of 114 Bersatu branch chiefs in Perlis signals a deepening crisis within the party that could have wider implications, an academic said.
Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) lecturer Muhammad Izmer Yusof said the development was not surprising, as Bersatu had limited strength when contesting on its own.
He said past election results showed the party had relied on the strength of its coalition partners.
"Before the 14th General Election (GE14) in 2018, Bersatu benefited from its cooperation with Pakatan Harapan, while after 2020, it relied on Pas's machinery.
"Even without the resignation of the 114 branch chiefs, the current crisis between Bersatu and Pas is enough to weaken the party because without support from a strong political partner, its prospects in future elections would be severely affected," he said when contacted yesterday.
On potential cooperation between Pas and Umno, Izmer said political dynamics were driven by common interests rather than permanent alliances or rivalries.
He said the biggest challenge would be seat allocation, particularly in the four states under the SG4 grouping — Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu — where Umno's electoral strength is limited.
He suggested that Pas and Umno could consider dividing constituencies according to their respective areas of influence, including allowing Pas and Perikatan Nasional to retain constituencies in the SG4 states, while BN focuses on Melaka, Johor and Negri Sembilan.
On the emergence of Wawasan, Izmer said the new party could seek to fill the political space left by Bersatu in Perlis and nationally.
He said Bersatu-held seats could potentially be contested by Wawasan candidates in future state or general elections.
The internal crisis in Bersatu Perlis began on July 9 when Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah resigned from the party's supreme leadership council, followed by state executive councillor and Sena assemblyman Marzita Mansor.
On the same day, Bersatu Perlis secretary and Senator Azahar Hassan announced his resignation from the party and all positions held.
The crisis continued on Aug 11 when another state executive councillor, Megat Hashirat Hassan, resigned as an Arau division committee member.
The situation escalated on Sept 8 when Padang Besar Bersatu deputy chief Ramzi Md Udi and 14 branch chiefs quit the party, followed by 90 Kangar division branch chiefs on Sept 9 and 10 Arau division branch chiefs the following day.

Title: 5,000 expected at BCCK for national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebration
Article:
KUCHING: About 5,000 people are expected to gather at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) tonight for the national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebration.
Sarawak is hosting the national celebration once again, having last held the event in 2023.
Programmes will begin at 7pm with a pre-show segment, followed by the arrival of guests from 7.30pm.
Guests of honour include Sarawak Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar and his wife Toh Puan Fauziah Mohd Sanusi, along with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor are also scheduled to attend.
The official ceremony begins at 8.15pm, featuring the prime minister's address, followed by the signing of the Malaysia Day Celebration Special Book.
The event will showcase performances by invited artistes, a musical theatre presentation, and a grand finale bringing together performers representing Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, and Sarawak.
The public in Kuching can also watch a fireworks display at the Kuching Waterfront as part of the closing segment.
Leading up to the main event, several activities were organised, including a Malaysia Day exhibition from Sept 10 to 16 at Plaza Merdeka.
Two thanksgiving ceremonies were also held, namely an interfaith thanksgiving prayer on Sept 14 at Hotel Pullman and a thanksgiving service on Sept 15 at the Sarawak State Jamek Mosque.

Title: Women's drug abuse cases rise by 3.3pct last year
Article:
KOTA BHARU: The number of women detected for drug abuse in the country rose to 8,926 last year from 8,638 in 2024.
National Anti-Drug Agency (NADA) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said youths aged 19 to 39 made up the largest group, with 6,193 cases, followed by adults aged 40 to 59 (2,567) and teenagers (166).
"Amphetamine-Type Stimulants were the most commonly used illicit drugs among women, involving 7,588 people, followed by opiates (762), cannabis (138), psychotropic pills (119) and others, including kratom and cocaine (319)," he said recently.
Ruslin said a report by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) found that women faced far more complex challenges than men in accessing treatment.
"Although statistics showed that women accounted for a lower percentage, at 4.7 per cent compared with 95.3 per cent for men last year, the barriers they faced were often systemic and emotional.
"Society tends to view drug addiction among women as a greater moral failure compared with men," he said.
He said women also often had more limited financial resources or were economically dependent on their partners.
"Treatment costs, such as transportation to NADA facilities, can be a heavy burden. UNODC reported that women faced difficulties accessing treatment if their partners were also drug addicts who controlled their movements or prevented them from making changes," he said.
Under the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983, following amendments that came into force on Aug 22, 2025, women can seek voluntary community-based treatment under the supervision of a Rehabilitation Officer or receive free treatment at the Narcotics Addiction Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen).
"We also provide AADK's Borderless Rehabilitation Treatment Mobilisation (MRT) service to rural areas, helping to overcome logistical constraints often faced by women," he said.

Title: Five held after obstructing enforcement team at Tasek Bera Ramsar site
Article:
BERA: Police detained five people, including four women, for allegedly obstructing an enforcement team during a joint operation at the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve (Ramsar) yesterday.
District police chief Superintendent Zulkiflee Nazir said the five allegedly obstructed and provoked enforcement personnel during the operation around 10am.
He said the operation involved several enforcement agencies and was conducted under the National Forestry Act 1984.
"During the operation, a group believed to be Orang Asli had set up barriers and provoked enforcement personnel. Five suspects were arrested," he said in a statement.
[[nid:1533782]]
Several videos of the operation at the forest reserve went viral on social media yesterday, showing enforcement personnel negotiating with a group of individuals to gain access to a section of the forest.
Zulkiflee said the case was being investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for voluntarily obstructing a civil servant in the discharge of public functions.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
The operation involved the Pahang State Enforcement Unit, Forestry Department, Bera District and Land Office, General Operations Force, Wildlife and National Parks Department and police.
The special operation, which began on Sept 14, was aimed at destroying illegal plantations and curbing land encroachment at the Tasek Bera forest reserve.

Title: Wall Street ends lower as oil spikes and the benchmark Treasury yield breaches 5pct
Article:
NEW YORK: Wall Street extended its selloff on Tuesday, as rising US Treasury yields, mounting debt concerns and soaring crude prices kept buyers on the sidelines.
All three major US stock indexes extended Monday's losses as broad risk-off sentiment weighed on nearly every sector but energy. That sector benefited from expanding hostilities in the Middle East, which included new attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.
"Given rising prices for fuel, especially diesel, given the near-certain outlook for rising rates beginning tomorrow, and given the concerns over the potential slowdown in the AI ecosphere, why step into the market aggressively until some of this clears up?" said Peter Tuz, president of Chase Investment Counsel in Charlottesville, Virginia.
The Federal Reserve has convened for its two-day monetary policy meeting, which is due to culminate on Wednesday with the central bank's rate decision. With recent economic data showing the labor market on solid footing, while war-related energy price pressures are morphing into broader, systemic inflation, the central bank is expected to implement a 25-basis-point increase to its Fed funds target rate — its first interest rate hike in over three years.
In the wake of last week's hot inflation data and the near 25 per cent jump in US crude prices over the last two weeks, financial markets have priced in more than a 95 per cent likelihood of a rate hike on Wednesday, up from 33.1 per cent one month ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Tuz added that while markets will learn the Fed's decision tomorrow, "the Middle East conflict is a wild card as to how long it might last."
Front-month West Texas Intermediate and Brent oil settled up 4.4 per cent and 2.9 per cent respectively, while diesel futures closed at a record high.
"This will probably be not a one-and-done, but a series of rate increases," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois. "It will be dependent on oil; that is really the source of inflation and it's starting to seep into other parts of the market."
As rate-hike bets increased, global bond yields resumed their upward climb, with benchmark US Treasury yields breaching 5 per cent and reaching the highest level since 2007.
Rising interest rates are increasing the pressure on heavily indebted borrowers, including companies that have placed big bets on AI.
Those worries exacerbated mounting fears over AI's destructive potential and growing opposition to the construction of data centers, which came to a head on Monday and dragged the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index down.
According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 34.47 points, or 0.45 per cent, to end at 7,585.51 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 202.84 points, or 0.77 per cent, to 25,983.58. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 330.74 points, or 0.63 per cent, to 52,090.46.
Dave & Buster's tumbled following the company's second-quarter revenue miss.
Waystar rose after Reuters reported the healthcare software firm is exploring options, including a potential sale.
Weakness in bitcoin was compounded by the US Senate not advancing comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation, in a blow to digital asset companies. Crypto firms Coinbase and Strategy closed sharply lower.

Title: Driver who rammed three vehicles tests positive for four drugs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A driver who rammed into three vehicles at a traffic light junction in Jalan Kampung Bandar Dalam yesterday was found to have tested positive for four different types of drugs.
City Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the crash occurred at 3.50pm two days ago.
Footage of the incident subsequently went viral on Threads, prompting traffic police to track down all the vehicles involved.
"All drivers were asked to report to the police station.
"Preliminary investigations revealed that a 30-year-old man driving a Honda Civic lost control of his car before crashing into three other vehicles," he said in a statement today.
Zamzuri said the crash was believed to have been caused by the Honda Civic driver losing control of his vehicle and driving recklessly.
"The three vehicles hit were a Proton Saga driven by a 46-year-old Algerian man, a Nissan Almera driven by a 46-year-old woman, and another Honda Civic driven by a 51-year-old woman.
"However, no injuries were reported in the incident," he said.
He said the Honda Civic driver went to the police station to lodge a report at 10.39pm yesterday.
"A breathalyser test conducted on the driver returned negative for alcohol.
"However, a urine screening conducted by the Dang Wangi district police headquarters Narcotics Crime Investigation Division found the driver positive for benzo, methamphetamine, ketamine, and amphetamine," he said.
He added that the case was being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and further investigations were ongoing.
Those with information can contact the Tun H S Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station.

Title: Japan bond yields extend gains on inflation concerns ahead of Fed decision
Article:
TOKYO: Japanese government bond (JGB) yields rose on Wednesday, extending gains as higher oil prices driven by the escalating Middle East conflict heightened inflation concerns ahead of the Federal Reserve's (Fed) interest rate decision.
Here are a few details:
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield rose 0.5 basis point (bp) to 3.035 per cent after hitting a fresh 30-year high on Tuesday. Yields move inversely to bond prices.
The 20-year JGB yield climbed 4 bps to 3.925 per cent. The 30-year yield added 4 bps to 4.190 per cent.
Oil prices hovered in the mid-US$100-a-barrel range after shipping industry sources said crude loadings at Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export hub of Yanbu had been suspended and Riyadh had cancelled some cargo deliveries to European customers.
Overnight, the yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose to 5.004 per cent after climbing to 5.041 per cent, its highest since July 2007.
The Fed will announce its policy ‌decision at 2pm EDT (1800 GMT) on Wednesday following the end of a two-day meeting.
Financial markets are betting heavily that the U.S. central bank will lift its benchmark rate a quarter of a percentage point, to a 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent range, and signal further tightening ahead.
At home, the Yomiuri newspaper reported that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is likely to retain Minoru Kiuchi as minister in charge of economic revitalisation in a cabinet reshuffle scheduled for Thursday.
Markets have been focusing on whether Kiuchi, an advocate of expansionary fiscal and monetary policy, would remain in his post for clues about whether the recent bond selloff might push Takaichi to rein in her spending plans. "In the bond market, many had viewed the possible replacement of Kiuchi as a buying factor, so some unwinding of those expectations could emerge today," said Keisuke Tsuruta, senior bond strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities.

Title: 40 districts nationwide record unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 40 districts nationwide recorded unhealthy air quality levels as of 8am today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 182.
Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) showed other badly affected areas included Cheras in Kuala Lumpur (179), Nilai in Negri Sembilan (178), Putrajaya (176), Shah Alam in Selangor (175), Seremban in Negri Sembilan (174), and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur (172).
All affected areas recording unhealthy air quality were in Peninsular Malaysia.
Meanwhile, 23 districts recorded moderate air quality, mostly in Sarawak, including Kuching (75), IPD Serian (73), Samarahan (70), and Sibu (66).
Sabah also recorded moderate air quality, including at Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (64), Keningau (56), and Sandakan (53).
Other locations with moderate readings included Alor Star (99) and Langkawi (96) in Kedah; Larkin (99) and Pengerang (98) in Johor; Kangar in Perlis (88); and Kota Bharu in Kelantan (88).
Only four districts in Sabah and Sarawak recorded good air quality levels, namely Sarikei (47), Limbang (46), Kota Kinabalu (45), and ILP Miri (44).
It was earlier reported that the number of hotspots detected in Kalimantan jumped to 808, increasing the risk of transboundary haze if open burning in Indonesia persists.
According to data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC),
hotspots in Kalimantan
rose from 301 on Sept 12 to 461 on Sept 13, before surging to 808 yesterday.
During the same period, ASMC also recorded 87 hotspots in Sumatra, 15 in Sabah and Sarawak, and one in Peninsular Malaysia.
The data highlighted a sharp increase in hotspots in Kalimantan over the two days, following lower counts earlier in the monitoring phase.

Title: Japan August imports jump as oil prices lift costs, exports stay firm
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's imports rose sharply for a third straight month in August as higher crude oil prices lifted energy costs, while exports rose for a 12th month in a row on resilient semiconductor-related demand, government data showed on Wednesday.
Total imports by value grew 28 per cent from a year earlier in August, Ministry of Finance data showed, compared with a median market forecast for a 26.3 per cent increase, as elevated crude oil prices boosted energy imports despite the yen's spike after a rare joint yen-buying intervention with the United States.
The trade figures underscore how higher energy prices are swelling import bills and fuelling inflationary pressures, reinforcing expectations the Bank of Japan will raise interest rates at the end of its two-day policy meeting on Friday.
Exports by value rose 19.3 per cent year-on-year in August, compared with economists' median forecast for an 18.2 per cent increase and following a 23.2 per cent rise in July, supported by strong chip-related shipments and higher non-ferrous metal prices.
Exports to the US rose 24.9 per cent in August from a year earlier, while those to China were up 20.6 per cent, the data showed.
Surging energy import costs kept Japan's trade balance in the red, with a deficit of 1.106 trillion yen (US$7.12 billion) in August, compared with economists' forecast for a deficit of 1.053 trillion yen.
Oil prices have risen further in recent weeks as attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure in the Middle East heightened concerns about supply disruptions, suggesting Japan's import costs could remain elevated in coming months.
Higher import costs, combined with solid exports and rising wages, could strengthen the case for additional rate hikes in the months ahead after a widely expected 25-basis-point hike on Friday, analysts said.
The BOJ may signal a faster pace of future rate hikes should price pressures heighten the risk of inflation overshooting its forecasts, sources familiar with its thinking have said.
Japan's economy has remained resilient despite the supply chain disruptions, with revised data last week showing growth in the April-June quarter was stronger than initially estimated, supported by business spending that proved more robust than previously reported.

Title: RM470bil investment target for Northern Corridor Economic Region by 2030 [WATCH]
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government has set a target for cumulative realised investment in the Northern Corridor Economic Region (NCER) to reach RM470 billion by 2030, RM126.2 billion more than the RM343.8 billion realised to date.
Key sectors including electrical and electronics (E&E), automotive, high-value tourism and modern agriculture are expected to account for 70 per cent of the targeted investment.
Northern Corridor Implementation Authority (NCIA) chief executive Datuk Mohamad Haris Kader Sultan said the region is confident of achieving the target, backed by approved investments expected to materialise over the coming years.
"We are confident that all those approved investments will be realised by 2030," he said at the launch of the NCER Strategic Development Plan 2026-2030 here today.
EV INVESTMENTS IN THE PIPELINE
As part of the push, NCER is exploring opportunities in the electric vehicle (EV) and automotive sectors to diversify its investment base beyond its established strength in E&E and semiconductors.
Mohamad Haris said several potential automotive investments are being assessed, although NCER has yet to determine how much the sector could contribute to the RM470 billion target.
"Among them are high-technology vehicle projects in Kulim, Kedah, with potential investors in the EV sector undergoing due diligence," he said.
NCER is working with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority and the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry to assess the potential investments.
So far, two investors have been identified in the EV battery segment, while three are being considered in the automobile segment.
E&E and semiconductors will remain the mainstay of investment in the region, particularly in Penang, where about 95 per cent of investments are expected to be concentrated in the sector.
In Kedah, Kulim Hi-Tech Park remains a key investment area, while semiconductor activities are also a major attraction at Chuping Valley in Perlis.
Mohamad Haris said the diversification push is aimed at spreading economic growth beyond established investment centres and into less-developed areas across Perlis, Kedah, Penang and Perak.
Programmes and projects will be implemented in these areas to create employment opportunities, including by ensuring that sites developed with allocations from the Economy Ministry are matched with approved investments.
Mohamad Haris said approved investments typically take between two and three years to translate into actual projects, although some could take up to five years.
"The target is higher than the previous plan, but the projection was supported by investment trends, and our targets for 2020 and 2025 had been exceeded," he said.
HIGH-SKILLED JOBS IN FOCUS
Beyond investment, NCER is targeting the creation of 310,000 jobs by 2030, with 45 per cent expected to be high-skilled positions.
Mohamad Haris said the focus is not merely on increasing the number of jobs, but on attracting higher-value industries that could generate greater productivity and value-added activities.
The region is also targeting the development of 8,000 talents through the NCER Technology Innovation Centre, alongside efforts to encourage participation in technical and vocational education and training (TVET).
NCIA is working with local universities, polytechnics, TVET institutions and industry players to identify the specific disciplines and skills required by investors.
The investment and employment push is expected to help lift the region's median household income to RM7,500 by 2030.
"To achieve the new targets, NCER would coordinate cross-government, ministry and agency cooperation to link investments with talent, technology, local enterprises and supply chains, creating broader economic value," Mohamad Haris said.
Meanwhile, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the strategic plan reflects the government's commitment to translating the 13th Malaysia Plan into regional development in a structured and high-impact manner.
He said the plan would serve as a catalyst to position NCER as a leader in high-value industrial investment and a global hub for research, development, commercialisation, technology and innovation.
"These targets are not merely numbers, but a reflection of our commitment to ensuring that every ringgit of investment coming into the region is translated into higher incomes, quality jobs and greater prosperity for the people of Perlis, Kedah, Penang and Perak," he said.
Under the plan, NCER is targeting regional gross domestic product of RM369 billion by 2030, compared with RM284.8 billion currently.
Among the long-term projects expected to transform the northern region's economic landscape are the Kedah Science and Technology Park, Sidam Logistics, Advanced Manufacturing and Aerospace Hub, Kedah Rubber City, Chuping Valley Industrial Area, Bagan Datuk industrial area, Penang Silicon Island and the Northern Peninsula border economic zone.

Title: Washington set to approve US$2.8bil arms package for Israel
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US federal government is on track to approve a US$2.8 billion arms package for Israel, US media reported Tuesday, with the sale of 40,000 one-ton bombs among the largest munitions packages sold in recent years.
The Washington Post said the package – funded with US taxpayer dollars – featured some of the most destructive munitions in Western arsenals, including 20,000 MK-84s, 20,000 BLU-117s, and 20,000 I-2000 Penetrator warheads.
The New York Times said the administration of US President Donald Trump had approved the sale, citing a US official.
A senior administration official told AFP that "all foreign arms sales are moving through the appropriate process," but wouldn't comment on pending transactions.
Meanwhile, a State Department spokesperson told AFP that "as a matter of policy, the Department does not confirm or comment on proposed arms sales until they have been formally notified to Congress."
The deal was reported amid an ongoing munitions shortage within the US military, with stocks rapidly depleting from the war with Iran and with the US spending US$22.3 billion on munitions between Feb 28 and June 30.
In February 2025, the Trump administration had approved the sale of more than US$7.4 billion in bombs, missiles and related equipment to Israel, including MK-84 munitions.
In response to concerns over civilian deaths in Gaza, former US president Joe Biden's administration had blocked a shipment of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel, but the Trump administration approved them after taking office in early 2025.

Title: Diverging fortunes of Hengyuan and Petron Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two Port Dickson-based refiners are seeing sharply diverging fortunes on Bursa Malaysia, with Hengyuan Refining Co Bhd outperforming Petron Malaysia Refining & Marketing Bhd as investors weigh their ability to benefit from elevated refining margins.
Hengyuan's shares have surged more than fourfold this year, with the refiner emerging as a major outperformer amid heightened US-Iran tensions.
The stock has jumped 353 per cent to RM3.49 from 77 sen on Jan 2 so far this year. From end of February, when the US-Iran conflict began, Hengyuan's share price has rallied by more than 250 per cent.
Since both companies reported their second-quarter (Q2) results on Aug 28, Hengyuan's share price has surged about 77 per cent to RM3.45 as at Sept 14, from RM1.95.
The rally accelerated alongside the renewed escalation in the US-Iran conflict on Sept 1.
Petron, meanwhile, saw its shares edge up only about 5.7 per cent to RM3.53 from RM3.34 over the same period.
The share price also has fallen about 9.0 per cent year to date from RM3.88 at the start of the year.
The stock initially gained during the February escalation, rising 10.6 per cent from RM4.15 to RM4.59.
It subsequently reached a 2026 peak of RM4.90 before retreating 31.8 per cent to RM3.34, although it has since recovered to RM3.53.
Petron's market capitalisation stood at about RM953 million.
The divergent share-price performance means Hengyuan has added roughly RM1.6 billion to its market value since the start of the year, while Petron's market value remains below RM1 billion.
Tradeview Capital fund manager Neoh Jia Man said the divergence comes as Hengyuan is able to capture the improving refining economics, while Petron Malaysia's operation continues to face disruptions following the collapse of its product jetty at its Port Dickson refinery last year.
"As a result, Petron is unable to fully capture the upside from the higher refining margins.
"In addition, unlike Hengyuan, Petron Malaysia has sizable fuel retail and commercial supply businesses, which dilute its overall exposure to the refining sector," he told the Business Times.
With the new jetty only targeted for commissioning in the first quarter (Q1) of 2027, Neoh said Petron's refinery operations remain constrained in the interim, requiring the company to rely primarily on imported refined products.
This limits its ability to fully benefit from the current refining-margin upcycle compared with Hengyuan, he said.
The diverging fortunes of the two listed oil refineries on Bursa Malaysia can also be seen through their financial results over the last two quarters.
In the first quarter ended March 31, 2026, Hengyuan staged a remarkable turnaround, chalking a net profit of RM525.55 million, from a net loss of RM170.45 million in the corresponding quarter.
Its net profits continued to increase in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, at RM600.54 million, a 14.3 per cent increase quarter-on-quarter. In the first half of the year, Hengyuan's net profits exceeded RM1.13 billion, compared with a net loss of RM353.7 million a year ago.
On the other hand, Petron Malaysia suffered a net loss of RM35.04 million in Q1 FY26, as production halted during the quarter due to the destruction of its product jetty following tropical storm Senyar in November 2025.
The group continues to chalk a net loss of RM34.5 million during Q2 FY26.
REFINERIES ENJOYING ELEVATED CRACK SPREADS
Crude oil refineries have been enjoying elevated crack spreads – the price difference between a barrel of crude oil and the average output of refined product – since the outbreak of the US-Iran war starting Feb 2026.
According to data compiled by Trading Economics, the crack spread index of US refineries stood at 62.36 points as of Sept 15, near the multi-year high of 70 points reached early this month.
While the spread has fallen 10.06 per cent over the past month, it is still 136.85 per cent higher than a year ago.
Neoh noted that Hengyuan is positioned to capture any further improvement in crack spreads, with the company having no major refinery turnaround scheduled until 2028.
Based on Tradeview Capital's estimates, he said Singapore's complex refining margin had moderated substantially in September but remained at an elevated level.
"We believe Hengyuan is well positioned to capture any further widening in crack spreads, given that it has no major refinery turnaround scheduled until 2028.
"Furthermore, only around 20 per cent of its crude supply is sourced from the Middle East, limiting its exposure to potential supply disruptions arising from the current geopolitical instability in the region," it said.
HOW MUCH LONGER WILL AN ELEVATED MARGIN STAY?
The conflict in the Middle East continues to disrupt the global oil trade as flow of the liquid through the Strait of Hormuz is interrupted, as both the US and Iran are unable to come to an agreement of a cease fire.
Iran's attack on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities, including the huge east-west oil pipeline, threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply. Meanwhile, the Islamic Republic's proxy – the Houthis in Yemen – have seized control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait – the only route to access the Suez Canal.
However, BIMB Securities Research noted that this escalatory cycle is unlikely to be sustained, due to logistics limitations for the US.
"Our bullish tilt on oil prices (US$110 to US$120 highs) is likely to reverse within a two to four week window, based on the previous patterns," said the research firm in a note on Sept 15.
The research firm reiterates its trading tilts on Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd, which is a direct proxy to oil prices, Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (benefitting from the higher fertilizer prices) and Hengyuan. The firm does not cover Hengyuan.
"Of the three, we see Hengyuan having the most room to surprise on the upside, including earnings, thanks to its exposure to the crack spreads.
"However, as highlighted earlier, we remain mindful that the current surge in oil prices is unlikely to persist – and likewise the catalyst for the stocks," the research firm noted.
It said that Hengyuan's windfall profit of RM1.1 billion in 1H FY26, which translates into an earnings per share of RM1.78, when annualised could reach around RM3.60 per share.
"Despite the 358 per cent YTD share price rally, this would still imply a price-earnings multiple of only around one time, suggesting that valuation remains undemanding relative to the prevailing earnings run rate.
"In our view, the key question is therefore not how far Hengyuan's share price has risen, but how long the current elevated crack spread environment can persist," the research firm said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysian firms tap Australia's multibillion-ringgit investment boom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Australia is becoming an increasingly important growth engine for Malaysian companies, as they tap billions of ringgit worth of opportunities spanning infrastructure, renewable energy (RE), mining and property.
The scale of that exposure is already significant for some Bursa Malaysia-listed firms such as Gamuda Bhd, which boasts more than one-third of its RM61.6 billion outstanding order book tied to Australian construction jobs.
CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd analysts Kenny Mak Hoy Ken and Wei Yi Tan said Australia's appeal as an investment destination is backed by favourable migration trends, opportunities for scalable operations and a sound business environment.
"The core investment focus of Malaysian corporates and government-backed entities in Australia is centred on the four sectors which continue to provide long-term value," they said in a note.
Infrastructure is among the areas where the scale of opportunity is particularly pronounced, with major spending programmes across several Australian states opening up potential work for Malaysian firms.
For Sime Darby Bhd's industrial arm, the opportunities include RM21 billion of spending ahead of the 2032 Brisbane Olympics, Sydney Metro's RM60 billion investment plan over the next four years and Western Australia's aim to attract RM160 billion in private investments over four years.
Gamuda, meanwhile, has established itself as one of Australia's leading Tier-1 contractors since entering the market in 2015, the analysts said.
Its Australian operations now employ about 2,500 people and span major rail, road and RE projects.
The company is currently undertaking the RM7.3 billion Sydney Metro West Stations Package West after winding down work on the RM6.5 billion Western Tunnelling Package.
It recently added the RM2.5 billion Parramatta Integrated Station Development, its third major Sydney Metro contract, in which Gamuda has an effective 80 per cent participation.
The latest win means Gamuda has secured six of the nine station packages along the Sydney Metro West line.
CIMB Securities expects the Parramatta station works to potentially generate pre-tax margins of up to eight per cent, compared with the typical five to six per cent for its conventional Australian infrastructure jobs.
The group is also part of a consortium shortlisted for a construction package under the Sydney-Newcastle high-speed rail project, whose overall cost is projected at up to AU$90 billion.
Australia's energy transition is opening another avenue for Malaysian capital.
The country is targeting RE to account for 82 per cent of electricity generation by 2030, requiring further private investment in generation, storage and transmission infrastructure.
Investment in utility-scale solar alone reached a record AU$3 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with AU$876 million in the second half of last year.
CIMB Securities said discussions with Malaysian infrastructure and utility players operating there pointed to an upbeat longer-term view of Australia's clean-energy transition.
"Leading the Malaysian charge in Australia's booming RE market are Gamuda and Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas)-backed Gentari Australia," it said.
Gamuda has already secured projects across solar, wind, hydro, battery storage and electricity transmission, while increasingly moving beyond construction into ownership of RE assets.
The company has raised its target for RE assets under development, construction and operation to five gigawatts (GW) by 2031.
This is after achieving its initial target of building a 1GW to 2GW portfolio by 2029, within two years of entering Australia's energy market.
Australian projects are expected to make up a substantial portion of the enlarged portfolio.
Petronas' Gentari is also building its Australian footprint.
Its RE portfolio currently comprises 422 megawatts (MW) of installed capacity, with another 571MW under management. Its flagship Maryvale project in New South Wales pairs a 243MW-peak solar farm with a 172MW battery energy storage system.
Property is emerging as another area of Malaysian interest, although developers are becoming more selective as Australia's broader residential market softens.
CIMB Securities said Malaysian developers were increasingly targeting purpose-built student accommodation, co-living and rental housing, particularly in Melbourne and Sydney.
"The Malaysian developers are focusing on the more resilient living sub-sectors such as purpose-built student accommodation as well as co-living accommodation schemes that offer flexible, community-focused living with shared amenities," it said.
The opportunity is driven by a shortage of student accommodation. Cushman & Wakefield estimates Melbourne alone could face a shortfall of as many as 200,000 student housing beds, based on 2023 enrolment levels.
Malaysian developers with projects or expansion plans in Australia include SP Setia Bhd, Sime Darby Property Bhd, UEM Sunrise Bhd, Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd, MRCB and Gamuda.
For CIMB Securities, Gamuda remains its preferred Malaysian stock for exposure to Australia's infrastructure and RE pipeline.
The research firm said the size of Gamuda's Australian order book underscored the country's growing importance to the group.
It said the RM61.6 billion record order book, of which Australian construction jobs account for 35 per cent, highlighted "Australia's strategic importance in sustaining Gamuda's order book replenishment trajectory.

Title: PH weighs going solo in Melaka polls as seat talks with BN hit impasse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Going solo has emerged as Pakatan Harapan's most strategic option for the upcoming Melaka state polls as cooperation with Barisan Nasional has reached an impasse, political analysts said.
This follows BN's firm stance to defend all 21 seats it won in the 2021 state election.
The issue escalated after acting Melaka PKR chief Adam Adli Abd Halim said PH was ready to contest all 28 state seats independently.
Ilham Centre executive director Hisommudin Bakar said the lack of progress in seat allocation left PH with no choice but to build its own electoral narrative ahead of the polls.
"Adam's statement is a clear signal that PH cannot afford to wait indefinitely for BN.
"PH must prepare its supporters early for the reality that political cooperation in Putrajaya will not automatically translate into a formal electoral alliance at the state level," he told the
New Straits Times
.
Hisommudin said, with BN holding a solid two-thirds majority, PH's primary focus must shift towards safeguarding its five incumbent seats held by DAP and Amanah, while strategically targeting a handful of mixed battlegrounds to preserve its regional influence.
On Sunday, Adam  said the party had to be prepared for the polls, adding that it was not as if PH had never contested all seats before.
"We must always be prepared because whether to negotiate or not is a choice, and every party has the right to decide.
"Contesting all seats will not be an issue for us."
Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Adam's declaration was  both a practical contingency plan and a calculated negotiating posture intended to pressure BN leadership into commencing formal talks on equitable terms.
"PH's strongest claim is for seats it currently holds or where it maintains a proven competitive record, particularly in urban and mixed constituencies."
He said deferring talks until after the state legislative assembly is officially dissolved would put PH at a severe disadvantage, potentially sparking sabotage and candidate friction due to a compressed campaign timeline.
He added that going solo presented a formidable challenge for PH, given the state's current political makeup.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities' Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said that current political indicators suggested that BN would rely on its established machinery, likely restricting PH's wins to between five and seven seats within Chinese-majority and urban mixed areas.
He said that while DAP retained  a firm footing in its traditional strongholds, PKR faced  a tougher battle to reclaim lost territory unless it successfully capitalises on urban middle-class sentiment over national issues.
"Current indicators suggest that BN could retain the number of seats it previously won. Although PH may not take over Melaka from BN, PH still stands a chance of winning at least seven state assembly seats in Chinese-majority and urban mixed constituencies.
"It might be more difficult for PKR to win seats compared with DAP."
The analysts also said that a direct contest between PH and BN in Melaka would  not threaten the stability of the unity government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Attempted Trump assassin ordered packages using Bob Dole's name, new records show
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Tuesday the FBI had discovered new information regarding the shooter who attempted to assassinate Donald Trump during a campaign event in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024.
"It is new information about the shooter and about his background, about his history and that stuff that we didn't know before," Blanche told reporters during a White House press conference, declining to elaborate.
A person who reviewed documents detailing the new information said it includes that the shooter had packages delivered to him under the pseudonym Bob Dole, the late Republican senator and presidential candidate.
The records also note that the shooter purchased parts and tools to increase his rifle's capacity from Amazon, the person said, who declined to be identified because the documents are not public.
An anonymous donor also paid to cremate the remains of the shooter, who was killed by a Secret Service sniper during the assassination attempt, which came as a total surprise to the family, according to the documents the person reviewed.
The gunman fired eight shots before he was killed, including one that grazed Trump's ear and one that killed a bystander and injured two others. Investigators still have not identified a motive, the person added.
The comments from Blanche came hours after Trump claimed on social media that new information was found about the assassination attempt and alleged without evidence that it was really a "Democrat Plot, to get me out of the Election."
Investigations into the shooting have found the shooter acted alone and produced no evidence Democrats had anything to do with the shooting.
Trump added that former FBI Director Christopher Wray, whom Trump appointed in his first term but later grew to hate, "should pay a price" for how the department responded to the assassination attempt "and certainly for the things he said."
Blanche, who was Trump's personal lawyer at the time of the assassination attempt, said during the briefing that he was with Trump as the investigation into the shooting was playing out, trying to ascertain what happened.
"His frustration and concern about what the former director was doing is something that is not new," Blanche said.
The Justice Department and FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment, and the White House referred to Blanche's comments. Wray could not be reached for comment.

Title: Armed Forces maps out 5D strategy to counter future threats [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  The armed forces are sharpening a strategy for the future with a five-pronged approach — from diplomacy and detecting threats early to deterring, denying and, if necessary, defeating them.
Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the strategy was aimed at ensuring the force remained credible and prepared to deal with threats across the land, sea, air, cyber and electromagnetic domains.
He said this year's 93rd Armed Forces Day theme, "Armed Forces' Resilience, the Nation's Defence Bastion" (
Ketahanan ATM, Benteng Pertahanan Negara
), reflected the importance of resilience in enabling the force to fulfil its core responsibility of safeguarding national security and sovereignty.
"Resilience is important because it determines whether the armed forces can fulfil the main duty of safeguarding the security and sovereignty of the country.
"Without resilience, trust in our ability to carry out that task may be weakened.
"Resilience is not limited to physical strength or military assets, but is built on three values under the 'ATM' approach – Akhlak Teras (Core Character), Tatakelola Tuntas (Comprehensive Governance) and Martabat Tempur (Combat Readiness)."
He said Akhlak Teras formed the foundation through the strength of character among personnel and formations.
Tatakelola Tuntas covered the management of people, assets, procurement and finances, with integrity, honesty, sincerity and trust at its core.
"After we have strong character and good governance, we have Martabat Tempur.
"This supports our mission to safeguard security and sovereignty and gives our stakeholders the assurance that we are ready to carry out our responsibilities."
THE 5D STRATEGY
Malek said the 5D strategy — Diplomacy, Detect, Deter, Deny and Defeat — provided the strategic approach for developing a credible "Future Force".
He said Diplomacy involved using diplomatic channels to reduce risks before resorting to other measures, while Detect focused on building the knowledge and early-warning capability needed to identify potential threats.
"Diplomacy is important because before we take physical action, we must first reduce the risk through diplomatic channels.
"Then, through Detect, we must know and understand the threat before it arrives or builds up its strength.
"The Detect component requires stronger detection, communications and intelligence systems, while Deter is aimed at imposing costs on potential threats and preventing them from escalating."
He said such costs could involve time, space, assets and sustainment, creating sufficient deterrence for anyone with hostile intent against Malaysia.
"When we talk about Deter, we must make sure the cost is there for the adversary — the cost in terms of time, space, assets and sustainment. You don't play around with Malaysia."
Malek said Deny involved preventing an adversary from achieving its objectives if it entered Malaysia's forward, extended or core areas, requiring the army, navy and air force to perform their roles across different operational domains.
He said Defeat would come into play if a threat reached the point where it had to be confronted, with the armed forces required to have the capability to defeat threats across all domains.
"If they enter, we must have the force to defeat them.
[[nid:1533727]]
"This is not only about cyber, electromagnetic, media and information warfare, but also air, sea and land combat. We have to be ready across all domains."
The 5D approach was not merely an aspiration, but formed part of the Future Force strategy for dealing with current and future threats until 2055, he said.
"This is not just a hope. We have made it the Future Force strategy to face whatever threats and situations that exist now and in the future.
"We have to look at what is expected through 2055 and make sure the force we develop is credible and capable of facing it."
He said the Future Force programme began in 2021, with its first phase focused on designing the force, including its structure, organisation and strategy, while identifying gaps and weaknesses.
The second phase, from 2026 to 2030, focuses on force development, with the ultimate aim of creating a credible joint force that can respond to future threats.
BUILDING THE FORCE FOR FUTURE THREATS
Malek said capability development under the 2026-2030 phase of the Future Force would focus on ensuring readiness translated into credible deterrence.
"Readiness is deterrence. If you want to do something bad to Malaysia, you should think two or three times, maybe 10 times, before you come."
For the army, he said, priorities included mobility, protection and firepower, with new vehicles and systems to replace ageing platforms.
He added that the force also needed improved mortar and artillery firepower, short-range and very short-range air defence systems, communications, logistics and ammunition.
"The conflicts that we see, whether in the Middle East or Ukraine, show us that air defence is important, especially against missiles and drones.
"We have to make sure our air defence capability can counter the threats that we may face."
For the Royal Malaysian Navy, capability development includes the Littoral Combat Ship, Littoral Mission Ship Batch 2 and Fast Interceptor Craft programmes.
Malek said the Multi-Role Support Ship was particularly important for moving troops and assets between the peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak and was expected to be considered under the 13th Malaysia Plan.
"It gives us the strategic mobility to move the force where it is needed."
He highlighted plans for a new naval base in Bintulu to support operations in the country's fourth maritime region and strengthen the navy's presence in the South China Sea.
For the Royal Malaysian Air Force, the next five years will focus on a modernisation exercise to replace obsolete fighter aircraft, with the FA-50M forming part of the replacement programme.
Malek said the air force was also pursuing a Medium Range Air Defence System programme and additional radar capabilities to address surveillance gaps, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
He said three Anka unmanned aerial systems (drones) had already been activated in Labuan to strengthen forward surveillance in Sabah and Sarawak, while additional units could be considered under the next phases of the 13th Malaysia Plan, subject to government approval.
"We already have three Ankas in Labuan and they are being used for forward surveillance.
"For additional units, the requirement has been submitted and we are waiting for the government's approval."
He said the Bintulu Bare Base would serve as a forward operating base, allowing aircraft to operate closer to areas of interest without having to return to the main base in Kuching.
He said the facility was expected to be completed in 2028.
"We need a forward operating base so that our aircraft can move forward and operate closer to the area of operations.
"They do not have to return all the way to the main base every time, so this gives us greater operational flexibility."
On Station Lima on Pulau Layang-Layang, Malek said the armed forces would continue to improve facilities and infrastructure, including to the jetty, while maintaining the presence and readiness needed to safeguard Malaysia's extended maritime area.
He said the overall objective was to ensure the armed forces could translate its strategy into operational capability across the country's forward, extended and core areas.
"We have to make sure whatever strategy we adopt, we have the capability to execute it.
"That is what the Future Force is all about — making sure we are ready for the threats of today and tomorrow."

Title: Cyber Force to become fourth Armed Forces service by 2030 [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The armed forces have established a nucleus team to spearhead the formation of a Cyber Force, which is targeted to become operational by 2030.
Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the fourth service was necessary as cyberspace and electromagnetic warfare had become critical domains in modern security and military operations, with regional neighbours and other countries already developing similar capabilities.
"Last year, we established the nucleus team as part of our future force planning. The team will plan and assess the steps needed to turn the Cyber Force operational.
"The Defence Ministry has agreed to our guidelines. The aim is to have an operational Cyber Force by 2030 to carry out its duties in this domain," he said in an exclusive interview with the
New Straits Times
for the 93rd Armed Forces Day.
He said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin  was expected to launch the nucleus team during the Armed Forces Day celebrations at the Lumut Naval Base on Saturday.
He said capability development in cyber and electromagnetic activities (CEMA) was underway, covering cyber operations, electronic warfare and spectrum management.
"These capabilities have been applied during Exercise Camar Kilat Series 2/26 to generate operational effects within the CEMA framework.
"The armed forces are also building a pool of CEMA specialists, with 60 air force officers and 17 from other ranks having attended related courses up to July."
In July, Khaled told the Dewan Negara that work was underway to establish the Cyber Force as the fourth service branch of the armed forces to counter threats from modern and cognitive warfare.
He said warfare had shifted from traditional physical combat to dominance in cyberspace and shaping public perception.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than 100,000 Armed Forces personnel declare assets amid corruption push [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  A total of 100,904 armed forces personnel have declared their  assets as the military tightens oversight of high-risk positions and strengthens safeguards against corruption and misconduct.
Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman told the
New Straits Times
that asset declarations had reached 97.53 per cent, while personnel  in high-risk positions, including those involved in procurement, equipment specifications and financial management, would face closer monitoring.
The measures come amid heightened scrutiny of the armed forces following controversies earlier this year, including corruption cases involving senior military officers and allegations of immoral activities at military camps, which prompted internal investigations.
Earlier this year, former armed forces chief Tan Sri Mohd Nizam Jaffar was charged with abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and bribery, while former army chief Tan Sri Muhammad Hafiz-uddeain Jantan and his wife were charged with money laundering.
Also in the dock were former Malaysian Defence Intelligence Organisation chief Lieutenant-General Datuk Mohd Razali Alias and Joint Forces Headquarters chief of staff Major-General Datuk Mohamed Fauzi Kamis, who were charged with criminal breach of trust over an unauthorised welfare fund investment.
"Asset declaration in the armed forces is given serious attention. It's a true manifestation of honesty and trustworthiness.
"We have achieved 97.53 per cent, involving 100,904 officers and personnel," said Malek.
"I have also redeclared my assets after being appointed armed forces chief. All service personnel, senior officers and unit commanders were required to declare their assets.
"My KPI (key performance indicator) is that by Sept 16, all commanders, from the unit level up to the highest level, will have declared their assets," he said in an exclusive interview with the
New Straits Times
for the 93rd Armed Forces Day.
Malek said the 2026-2030 Anti-Corruption Action Plan had been implemented, while the Integrity and Anti-Corruption Plan was being developed to strengthen governance and corruption prevention.
He said officers holding high-risk positions would be reviewed within 18 months, with commanders and senior officers assessing their suitability and effectiveness in the posts.
"If they are no longer suitable, they will be transferred.
"But if they are effective and still required based on their subject matter expertise, commanders can recommend that they remain in the position, subject to the highest level of integrity monitoring."
He said the approach was to ensure officers in sensitive positions remained under continuous scrutiny, rather than relying solely on fixed-term rotations.
He said governance compliance would be continuously monitored by the Defence Ministry's Integrity Unit and governance monitoring units at the respective service headquarters.
These include the inspector-general departments at the Armed Forces Headquarters and the army, navy and air force, alongside auditors and audit officers at field formations.
Malek added that checks and balances were further strengthened through the Malaysian Armed Forces Standard Management Audit, including unannounced audits.
"Governance involving assets, finances, security and human resources must remain transparent and comply with regulations, with every audit finding requiring immediate corrective action and improvements.
"A total of 105,536 officers and personnel, or 98.7 per cent of the total active workforce, have also completed the Anti-Corruption Pledge, while integrity modules have been conducted for 4,240 personnel at 26 training centres."
He said moral and spiritual development of personnel was also being strengthened, with character-building part of the effort.
He said this included the 3T module — Takhalli, Tahalli and Tajalli — which focuses on removing negative traits and practices, instilling good values and character and translating values into actions and exemplary conduct.
He said the armed forces also strengthened the Islamic Spiritual Division, formerly known as the Armed Forces Religious Corps (Kagat), by placing it under his purview to give it greater organisational weight.
"A dedicated cell has also been established to address the spiritual welfare of non-Muslim personnel according to their faiths.
"Kagat officers were exposed to strategic thinking and defence studies, including through greater participation in staff colleges, so that they can contribute beyond religious duties and bring a spiritual and ethical perspective to wider organisational and strategic matters.
"We do not want our religious officers to become only
tok siak
,
tok bilal
or imam.
"I want them to develop strategic thinking so they can contribute to building the armed forces, together with strong human capital grounded in spirituality."

Title: South Korean workers challenging Trump administration over Georgia raid
Article:
BARCELONA: More than 300 South Korean workers who were detained in last year's immigration raid at a Hyundai electric-vehicle manufacturing plant in Georgia are challenging the US government, CNN reported on Tuesday.
US authorities arrested hundreds of workers, most of whom are South Korean nationals, in the raid at the Hyundai-LG battery project last September.
Administrative claims on behalf of the workers, a mandatory step before a federal lawsuit, have started to be filed with nine federal agencies, the CNN report said, citing a lawyer representing the claimants.
The Department of Homeland Security, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, the FBI and the Departments of Justice and Labor were among the agencies, it added.
"ICE Homeland Security Investigations, in coordination with our law enforcement partners, executed a judicial search warrant as part of an ongoing criminal investigation into allegations of unlawful employment practices and other serious federal crimes," a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security told Reuters on Tuesday.
"This investigation is focused on ensuring accountability for those who violate the law and upholding the rule of law," added the spokesperson, who did not comment directly on the reported challenge.
Hyundai did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside regular business hours.
The raid targeting the Georgia plant, operated through a joint venture between Hyundai and South Korea's LG Energy Solution, was described as the largest single-site enforcement operation in the Department of Homeland Security's history.
Video and photos of the incident showed workers shackled at the wrists, waist and ankles, images that shook South Korea, a key US ally.
Workers' phones were confiscated, and some were unable to inform their families back home until their eventual release.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US curbs S. Africa visas, alleging 'race-based discrimination'
Article:
WASHINGTON: The United States on Tuesday announced new restrictions on visas for South Africans, after President Donald Trump repeatedly criticised the country's leaders over its post-apartheid racial justice policies.
Trump has lambasted South Africa's land and employment laws that are meant to redress stark inequalities that remain 30 years after the end of white-minority rule.
In 2025, he berated President Cyril Ramaphosa in the Oval Office over discredited claims of a "white genocide" in South Africa. He has also hit the country with high tariffs and boycotted a G20 summit in Johannesburg.
The new visa restrictions target South Africans who "enable uncompensated land seizures, race-based discrimination, and/or the incitement of imminent violence against members of minority ethnic or racial groups," the US State Department said.
Ties between the two nations have nosedived since Trump took office last year, with the US leader cutting aid, expelling the South African ambassador and offering "refuge" to South African whites fleeing "persecution."
While the US president has cracked down on immigration, he launched a scheme under which thousands of white Afrikaners have been allowed to settle in the United States.
South Africa said last month it would offer a "generous" new trade deal to the United States as it seeks to avoid hefty tariffs that threaten massive job losses on top of its dire unemployment crisis.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After Gunung Kinabalu, porter conquers Chamonix ultra-trail
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
AFTER more than a year of training for one of the world's toughest ultra-trails, Gunung Kinabalu porter Daved Simpat crossed the finish line in Chamonix, France — carrying far more than just a personal achievement.
The 44-year-old completed the gruelling 174km Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc in 28 hours, 53 minutes and four seconds last month.
The feat reflects the strength, discipline and perseverance Daved developed while carrying climbers' loads up and down the mountain.
"Gunung Kinabalu has shaped me and is part of my life," he told the 'New Straits Times'.
At 4,095m above sea level, Gunung Kinabalu has served as Daved's workplace and training ground for most of his adult life.
The same principles he adopted for Gunung Kinabalu apply to ultra-trail — knowing when to run and when to walk, conserving energy and, most importantly, refusing to give up when the going gets tough.
As the first of seven Malaysians to cross the finish line after almost 29 hours, his thoughts turned to family, friends and those who had supported him.
The father of two from Kampung Himbaan in Ranau hopes his achievement inspires fellow porters and Sabah's youngsters.
Daved takes pride in his roots as a porter and does not view it merely as a stepping stone to becoming an international athlete.
"I want to show that our background is not a barrier. From a mountain in Sabah, a porter can also stand on one of the biggest ultra-trail stages in the world."
Daved said he was proud to bring the names of Sabah and Malaysia to the international stage.
He believes Sabah has much to offer — from its mountains and forests to its talented people and untapped potential.
His message to the young people in Sabah is simple: dream big, regardless of where you come from or what you do for a living.
For Daved, going from carrying heavy loads on Gunung Kinabalu to completing one of the world's toughest races proves that hard work, confidence and perseverance can take you further than you ever imagined.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Colombian president fires national statistics chief
Article:
BOGOTA: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella fired his statistics chief after the official ruled out inconsistencies in unemployment figures under the previous government, the former director said Tuesday.
De la Espriella took office in August and has accused his predecessor Gustavo Petro, Colombia's first-ever leftist leader, of corruption.
The president announced the dismissal of Ricardo Valencia as head of the national statistics agency (DANE) in a statement on Monday, barely three weeks after appointing him.
"I didn't have any communication from the presidency or from the president expressing any dissatisfaction," Valencia told Bogota-based Blu Radio on Tuesday.
A remark at a press conference cost him his job, it turned out.
Valencia responded to a journalist's question saying that he had not found any inconsistencies in labour market indicators during July, when Petro was still president.
"Up until the date when they asked me that question, I had not found any irregularities," the economist said.
De la Espriella has made it compulsory for all ministries and government agencies to seek permission from the presidency before providing any information to the press.
The presidency criticised Valencia for claiming not to have found "any irregularities" in the data "without having first carried out thorough audits."
Following the dismissal of their director, the DANE workers' union on Tuesday voiced concern about the agency's independence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze situation may worsen as Kalimantan hotspots rise to 808
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
THE number of hotspots detected in Kalimantan has surged to 808, which may cause transboundary haze to spread in the region.
Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said this depended on the extent of open burning in Indonesia and wind conditions.
"As long as the fires are not extinguished, the haze situation will continue to affect neighbouring countries.
"We are in the southwest monsoon period, during which winds blow from Indonesia towards our country. It is expected to end only in October."
Data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed that the number of hotspots in Kalimantan rose from 301 on Saturday to 461 the next day before surging to 808 on Monday.
During the same period, ASMC also recorded 87 hotspots in Sumatra, 15 in Sabah and Sarawak, and one in Peninsular Malaysia.
However, it said humid conditions expected in western Sarawak this week could potentially reduce the impact of transboundary haze.
ASMC said satellite imagery from the United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration helped to detect hotspots.
However, those could go undetected due to cloudy conditions or during gaps in satellite coverage, it added.
Meanwhile, Hisham said air quality could improve with the change in wind direction due to the onset of the northeast monsoon.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bessent defends Trump economic policies, reveals plans to meet Chinese official
Article:
WASHINGTON: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended a range of Trump administration economic policies before lawmakers on Tuesday, from currency and bond market interventions to AI safety, disclosing plans to meet with his Chinese counterpart this weekend.
Bessent told a hearing of the House Financial Services Committee that US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping would continue discussions next week on Iran and China's financial links to Teheran. Washington has been seeking to shut Iran out of Western financial systems as the Iran war stretches into its seventh month.
The hearing was nominally on the international finance system, including reforms to the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, but lawmakers peppered Bessent with questions about more pressing issues, such as the state of financial markets and the economy, and the administration's financial measures against Iran.
As the hearing got under way, several protesters stood up one after another to call for an end to sanctions on Iran and the war, forcing Bessent to stop and restart his opening statement. The people were hustled from the room.
Bessent told reporters rising bond yields were due to "global issues," as he headed into the hearing. The US 10-year Treasury yield hit peaks on Tuesday not seen since 2007 amid a global bond rout experienced by most other large economies.
Analysts tie the US bond yield increase to higher oil prices and expectations the Federal Reserve will raise its policy rate this week, as well as competition for capital from AI spending and concerns about the US fiscal trajectory.
During the hearing, Bessent acknowledged the rise in the 10-year yield reflects "the need to address the deficit," among other factors.
US bond yields have risen despite the Treasury's decision to double the size of longer-term debt buybacks that Bessent has described as a way to inject liquidity and counter the rise in yields, or at least slow it down.
Bessent told lawmakers the buybacks were successful in keeping yields from rising more, and that they underscored US credibility.
"There is a counterfactual of what would it have done — and we then proceeded to have the two most successful Treasury auctions that we've had in 20 years," Bessent told the congressional hearing. "Since President Trump has come in, (the US bond market) has been the best-performing bond market in the developed world."
He also defended the Treasury's joint intervention with Japan to shore up its currency, saying the US purchased a "nominal amount" of yen to signal support for Japanese policies, and made tens of millions of dollars in the process.
"A stronger yen is better for American exports. A stronger yen means that the Japanese government will not have to sell US assets to finance foreign currency intervention," Bessent added.
BESSENT HIGHLIGHTS FALLING POVERTY RATE
Several Democratic lawmakers pressed Bessent on the state of the economy, inflation and the rising cost of living — tying it to the Iran war and the run-up in global oil prices. Bessent blamed inflation on the previous Biden administration, and said Americans are better off under Trump.
He pointed to fresh data from the US Census Bureau showing that the percentage of Americans in poverty last year dipped 0.5 percentage point to the lowest rate on record, 10.2 per cent, with 34.5 million Americans in poverty. Median household income increased 2.6 per cent last year to a record US$87,460.
Bessent was also asked if Trump's proposal to pay each American US$5,000 if the Republican Party maintains congressional majorities in the November elections was serious. He said he would work with House Speaker Mike Johnson to make those payments happen if congressional approval proved necessary.
Bessent said the US dollar's strength reflects the Trump administration's credibility.
"A strong dollar is not a price on a screen; it is a set of behaviours, and what we have seen in this administration, where we are creating regulatory certainty, tax certainty, trade certainty and energy certainty that is bringing in trillions of dollars into the US," Bessent said.
AI SAFETY CONCERNS
Democrats questioned Bessent on concerns over increasingly powerful AI models after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow the rate of advancement to ensure their safety — sentiments echoed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Elon Musk, who runs xAI.
Asked about the administration's position on this, Bessent said the Treasury has "been working on safety nonstop since the release of Mythos" earlier this year, working with banks to share patches for cybersecurity software vulnerabilities exposed by the Anthropic model.
He said the administration forced Anthropic to withdraw a model for safety checks, and that AI labs should be held accountable for their creations, but it was important to stay ahead of China in the AI development race.
"I can tell you what we shouldn't do on safety is to give these labs a liability exemption, which is what they are asking for," Bessent said. "The best way to guarantee safety is that the creators are liable for what they build and generate, and put out into the economy and to the American people and to the world populace."

Title: Empty seats as schools reopen in Venezuela's quake-hit Guaira
Article:
LA GUAIRA: Schools in Venezuela's quake-scarred coastal state of La Guaira were deserted on Tuesday, a day after the start of the new school year, with many parents opting to keep children home for fear of further deadly tremors.
La Guaira, home to a popular resort of the same name north of Venezuela's capital Caracas, was devastated by powerful back-to-back quakes on June 24 that left over 6,500 people dead.
Dozens of schools were damaged in the worst disaster in the Caribbean country in decades, which reduced hundreds of buildings to rubble.
A further 60 schools were converted into shelters for thousands of people left homeless by the magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 quakes.
In some areas, lessons are being taught under a tarp.
In one such tented school on Tuesday, a teacher drew a circle on a blackboard as part of a discussion with 14 students on managing their emotions.
"They're still very sensitive. In any conversation you have with them, they always bring it (the earthquake) up, and it's always good to listen to them so they can process all that pent-up emotion," María Herrera, the 43-year-old teacher, explained to AFP.
Many parents were too fearful of a repeat disaster to allow their children back into a bricks-and-mortar classroom.
[[nid:1533701]]
Just over 300 students have enrolled for the new school year at John Paul II Diocesan Educational Unit, one of the few schools open in the port city of La Guaira.
The school has capacity for more than double that.
Only seven children showed up on Tuesday.
"The return to classes will be gradual and safe, focusing primarily on the emotional well-being not only of our students but also of our staff," said the principal, Marco Antonio Espinoza.
Yanet Dominguez, a fifth-grade teacher at the school, said parents had been plying her with questions about the building's structural safety.
"I told them yes, that improvements have been made to the building this year, and that they shouldn't be afraid to send their children," she said.
Amni Nunez, a 40-year-old industrial engineer, sent his two young children back to school after deciding that life must go on.
"They need to understand that the world keeps spinning and that we have to learn to live with this new reality," he told AFP.

Title: 'Overweight' call stays on healthcare
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Malaysia's healthcare sector could gain traction, driven by its low cost, ease of access and ability to provide personalised responses to patients.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB Research) cited a Boston Consulting Group (BCG) survey showing that a majority of adults polled across 15 countries in November 2025 had already used generative AI tools for health-related issues.
It added that an OpenAI survey in December 2025 found that three in five adults in the United States had used AI tools for health-related questions in the preceding three months.
"While there is currently limited data on Malaysians' use of large language models (LLMs) for healthcare-related queries, we take reference from the other regions as an indication of the potential trend in Malaysia," HLIB Research said in a note.
According to the BCG survey, higher-income individuals were substantially more likely to use LLMs for healthcare-related purposes.
The firm said the use of LLMs as a first point of consultation could have meaningful implications for hospital demand, particularly by breaking the "wait and see" mentality among patients.
HLIB Research said LLMs allow patients to better understand the potential significance of their symptoms and determine appropriate next steps, which could prompt them to seek professional care earlier and increase demand for healthcare services.
It said the potential was particularly relevant in Malaysia, where many health conditions remain under-diagnosed.
HLIB Research said the growing use of LLMs for healthcare queries could provide a more immediate tailwind for Malaysian hospital operators, such as IHH Healthcare Bhd, Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd and KPJ Healthcare Bhd.
Its top picks are IHH, with a target price of RM9.10, and KPJ, with a target price of RM3.79.
The firm maintained its "neutral" call on the healthcare sector.
