Title: Former Philippines leader Duterte due in ICC courtroom to assess if fit for murder trial
Article:
THE HAGUE: Former Philippines president Rodrigo Duterte is expected to appear in public for the first time on Wednesday since being transferred to the International Criminal Court 18 months ago to face murder charges related to his war on drugs.
Duterte, 81, served as president from 2016 to 2022, before being charged with crimes against humanity for creating, funding and arming death squads that targeted narcotics peddlers and users. He was arrested and taken to The Hague in March 2025.
On Wednesday, judges will hear arguments about his health and ability to stand trial, which is scheduled to begin in November. His lawyers have argued that he suffers from cognitive decline and is not well enough.
Duterte's lawyer and family did not respond to requests for comment.
ICC judges said in January that Duterte's health was good enough for him to follow proceedings and requested his presence in court, rather than by video link from the detention unit.
Duterte's warrant says he was responsible for a widespread and systematic campaign that led to thousands of killings between 2011 and 2019, including when he served as mayor of the southern Davao city.
ICC prosecutors have said as many as 30,000 people may have been killed in the crackdown, the details of which were reported in a Reuters investigation.
According to police, 6,200 suspects were killed during anti-drug operations. Duterte said he instructed police to act in self-defence and told supporters he was ready to "rot in jail" if it meant ridding the Philippines of illicit drugs.

Title: Trump slams Supreme Court over 'horrible' mail-in ballot ruling
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump blasted the Supreme Court on Tuesday after it blocked his divisive plan to restrict mail-in ballots, launching a rare and blistering attack on the justices he hand-picked in his first term.
Trump accused the conservative-dominated court of allowing itself to be cowed by Democrats and said it had delivered some of the most "destructive, hurtful, and damaging decisions in our Country's history."
The president did not name the justices but singled out the ones he had nominated in his first spell in the White House – Amy Coney Barrett, Brett Kavanaugh and Neil Gorsuch – for special criticism.
"These are not the people I interviewed to serve on the United States Supreme Court, they are merely a shell of their original selves," Trump said on his Truth Social network.
"The Supreme Court has really let our Country down! Certain Justices are petrified of these crazed and depraved Democrats, and are totally unable to show the courage necessary to save our America."
On Monday, the Supreme Court dealt Trump a major blow ahead of November's midterm elections when it denied his request to lift an order halting his plan to limit mail-in voting.
Republican Trump signed an executive order in March seeking to restrict mail-in voting, saying without evidence that it is vulnerable to fraud. The order quickly prompted multiple legal challenges.
Trump admitted it was rare for the US president, who heads the executive branch of the US government, to criticise the Supreme Court, which heads the judicial branch.
"It is not easy for me to write this criticism of the United States Supreme Court – it will likely cost me dearly for years to come – but I feel it my obligation and duty, as President, to do so for the America we love!"
- 'HORRIBLE' -
The Supreme Court ruled that there was not enough time to implement the restriction on mail-in ballots.
Justice Kavanaugh, in a concurring opinion with the majority, said Trump's plan may ultimately be legal in the long run, but "state and local election officials do not have sufficient time to reasonably implement the rule before the elections."
Only two of the six conservative justices – Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito – on the nine-member panel offered a dissent.
Trump called the decision itself "horrible" and "highly political."
Democratic-led states sued the administration on grounds that under the US Constitution, states – and not the federal government – retain broad control over the administration of elections.
"Trump's scheme was so on-the-nose, so un-American, so flagrantly unconstitutional that the MAGA Court had no choice but to make the right call," Democratic Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Tuesday.
More than 30 countries worldwide offer citizens the opportunity to vote using a mail-in ballot.
"It is a big loss for Republicans, and America itself, and makes cheating by the Radical Left 'Dumocrats,' on Mail-In Ballots, a much easier thing to do - And now they have an open field to do so!" Trump wrote.
The president has repeatedly denounced mail-in voting as corrupt – despite using it himself, including to vote in Florida's Republican primary just last month.
The fight, alongside disputes over partisan redistricting in around a dozen states, comes with high political stakes ahead of the Nov 3 elections.
Republicans hold narrow congressional majorities, but Democrats are favored to capture the House and possibly the Senate as Trump's approval ratings remain weak and voters voice frustration over living costs and the continuing war with Iran.
Losing control of Congress could not only stymie Trump's legislative agenda in the final two years of his presidency, but also expose him to investigations and even a third impeachment.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US Supreme Court deals blow to Trump's mail-in voting restrictions
Article:
WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court dealt a major blow Monday to President Donald Trump's attempts to restrict mail-in voting before the November midterm elections, denying his request to lift an order halting the divisive plan.
Only two of the six conservative justices on the nine-member panel offered a dissent.
Justice Brett Kavanaugh, in a concurring opinion with the majority, said Trump's plan may ultimately be legal in the long run, but "state and local election officials do not have sufficient time to reasonably implement the rule before the elections."
After the decision came down, Democratic Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said the president's "plan to make it harder to vote was obviously unconstitutional. The Supreme Court had no choice but to make the right decision."
His counterpart in the House, Hakeem Jeffries, said the court had blocked Trump's "diabolical scheme" to restrict mail-in ballots. "Democracy won. And far-right extremists lost," he posted on X.
Several states, including North Carolina, have already begun sending mail-in ballots to voters.
Trump signed an executive order in March seeking to restrict mail-in voting, saying without evidence that it is vulnerable to fraud. The order quickly prompted multiple legal challenges.
Democratic-led states sued the administration on grounds that under the US Constitution, states – and not the federal government – retain broad control over the administration of elections.
- USPS WHISTLEBLOWER -
Trump's executive order would require the compilation of lists of eligible voters and for the US Postal Service (USPS) to deliver ballots only to voters who are on the lists.
The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) hailed the Supreme Court's decision as a "major win for voting rights, election integrity, and democracy."
"This administration keeps testing the limits of its power, as if the rules governing our elections are merely suggestions to ignore when they don't suit the president's agenda," said Sophia Lin Lakin, director of the ACLU Voting Rights Project.
"The president does not run our elections, the Postal Service does not get to decide whose ballot counts, and voters – not the White House – will decide November's elections."
Officials from several states had warned that a lack of legal clarity around the plan was sowing chaos months before the Nov 3 vote.
A USPS whistleblower had also warned that millions of Americans may not receive ballots because the systems being used by the postal service have been put together in a "sloppy and rushed manner."
Trump has long been a critic of mail-in ballots but has frequently used them himself, including when he voted by mail in Florida's Republican primary earlier this year.
The president has for years claimed without evidence that mail-in voting is highly vulnerable to fraud, repeatedly linking it to his false assertion that the 2020 presidential election was stolen from him by Democrat Joe Biden.
Polls show that Trump's Republican Party faces a serious threat of losing its narrow control of Congress in November, particularly the House of Representatives.
If Democrats win, they have signaled they would block Trump's agenda and could even move to impeach him for the third time.--AFP

Title: National interests must transcend racial, religious differences, says Aaron
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysians need to continue strengthening their sense of belonging and shared identity in the effort to build a strong nation-state, with national interests surpassing racial, religious and regional differences.
National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said that in conjunction with the 63rd Malaysia Day celebration, the people are also urged to continue respecting one another, sharing common values, and preserving the unity and harmony that are the foundations of the country’s peace, stability and prosperity.
“After 63 years, the diversity of races, religions, cultures, languages, and customs in Malaysia continues to be a treasure and strength of the nation. From Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah and Sarawak, each community contributes to Malaysia’s unique and rich face.
“However, behind all the differences, we share the same identity, we are Malaysians. This sharing of identity is the foundation of the country’s peace, stability nd prosperity,” he said in a Facebook post.
Aaron said that despite diversity, all citizens share a common identity as Malaysians, which in turn becomes an important foundation in building the country’s future together.
The formation of Malaysia on Sept 16, 1963, was the result of a process of negotiation and mutual understanding that began with a proposal put forward by Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj in 1961, followed by the Cobbold Commission, the Inter-Governmental Committee and a series of negotiations.
The process also involved figures such as Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, Tun Fuad Stephens, Tun Datu Mustapha Datu Harun, Temenggong Jugah Anak Barieng and Stephen Kalong Ningkan, whose contributions became among the foundations of the nation’s formation.
“Happy Malaysia Day 2026. Malaysia belongs to all of us and Malaysia is our shared responsibility,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Wan Junaidi calls for mature, inclusive Malaysia as nation marks Malaysia Day
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 16 — Malaysia Day should serve as a national platform for reflection to assess how far the country has succeeded in building a mature, capable and magnanimous society in facing the challenges of the times.
The Yang Dipertua Negeri of Sarawak, Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar, said the strength of a nation is not measured solely by economic progress or physical development, but also depends on maturity and wisdom in managing its diversity.
“Malaysia today is entering an era that demands new ways of thinking. Global competition is becoming increasingly complex, driven by artificial intelligence, the digital economy and geopolitical changes.
“In this situation, we cannot merely be consumers of change. Instead, we must be the creators of the future,” he said in his message in conjunction with the 2026 Malaysia Day celebration today.
Wan Junaidi said Malaysia Day also served as a reminder that true progress could only be achieved when no one was left behind in the nation’s development.
He said the elderly, persons with disabilities, rural communities and vulnerable groups must continue to be given attention so that they too could enjoy the fruits of the nation’s prosperity.
“I also call for a culture of excellence to be continuously fostered in every field, whether in education, research, sports, the arts or public service. We must always strive to achieve the best standards at the international level.
“I also wish to see more young Sarawakians emerge as scientists, engineers, founders of technology companies, researchers, social entrepreneurs and community leaders,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya Immigration detains 173 foreign nationals at Sepang construction site
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The Putrajaya Immigration Department (JIM) detained 173 foreign nationals during an enforcement operation at a construction site for a hangar, warehouse bay and aircraft engine testing facility in Sepang, near here, today.
The operation was carried out following public complaints and a week of intelligence gathering in the area near a motorsports complex.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said 88 officers of various ranks were deployed to conduct inspections at the site.
He said 261 individuals, comprising 217 foreign nationals and 44 locals, were checked during the operation.
“The inspections also involved checks on workers employed by subcontractor companies involved in the project,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Zakaria said the operation resulted in the arrest of 173 foreign nationals, aged between 23 and 40, for suspected offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63 (Act 155) and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
Of the total, he said 147 were Bangladeshi men, 17 Indonesian nationals and nine Pakistani nationals.
Zakaria said employers were found to have hired foreign nationals using Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) issued to other companies, while also misusing Social Visit Passes to deceive the authorities.
He said five Form 29 (Witness Summonses) were issued to locals to assist in the investigation, while the foreign nationals involved were taken to the KLIA Immigration Detention Depot for further investigation and action.
Zakaria said immigration monitoring and enforcement would continue across all sectors, including the construction and logistics industries, as well as aviation industry support facilities.
“Action will be taken against any party found to be violating immigration laws, including employers or those who hire and harbour illegal immigrants,” he said. — Bernama

Title: More than 2.6 million Malaysians visited Indonesia in 2025 as neighbours gear up for 70 years of diplomatic ties
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 16 — Malaysia and Indonesia are looking forward to the 70th anniversary of their diplomatic relations in 2027, as bilateral cooperation between the close neighbours and strategic partners continues to gain momentum.
Malaysia’s Chargé d’Affaires to Indonesia Farzamie Sarkawi said this at the Malaysia Day celebration hosted by the Embassy of Malaysia in Jakarta, here on Tuesday night, highlighting the unique relationship between the two countries, which share history, language, and culture.
“We are not only neighbours, but also brothers and sisters who share history, language, and culture,” he said in his remarks, adding that the strength of Malaysia-Indonesia relations has enabled both countries to address obstacles and challenges through dialogue, mutual respect, and a spirit of friendship and togetherness.
The celebration was attended by Malaysia’s Ambassador-designate to Indonesia Datuk Muzaffar Shah Mustafa; Indonesia’s Higher Education, Science and Technology Minister Brian Yuliarto; Coordinating Minister for Law, Human Rights, Immigration, and Corrections Yusril Ihza Mahendra, and Home Affairs Minister Muhammad Tito Karnavian.
Farzamie said bilateral cooperation continues to gain momentum, with trade reaching US$34.22 billion (US$1=RM4.08) in 2025, while Malaysia remained Indonesia’s fourth-largest investor with investments amounting to US$4.5 billion.
He said people-to-people connections also remained strong, with more than 2.63 million Malaysian tourists visiting Indonesia last year, making Malaysia the largest source of foreign visitors to the republic, while 4.26 million Indonesian tourists visited Malaysia.
Farzamie said the leaders of both countries maintained close working and personal relations. This was reflected in the Annual Consultation between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and President Prabowo Subianto in Jakarta last year and Anwar’s special visit to the Indonesian capital on March 27 this year.
He said Malaysia and Indonesia also successfully convened the 17th Joint Commission for Bilateral Cooperation in Jakarta in June and the fourth Joint Trade and Investment Committee meeting this month.
On Asean, Farzamie said Malaysia remained committed to working closely with all Asean member states  to ensure that the regional grouping remains a strong, united, and influential force for peace, stability, and prosperity in the region.
Meanwhile, Brian in his remarks said education has long been an important pillar of Indonesia-Malaysia cooperation, with both countries continuing to strengthen cooperation through established frameworks and commitments since the signing of a joint agreement in education and culture in 1972.
“I believe that the establishment of a joint Indonesia-Malaysia academic consortium under this framework will further deepen collaboration among our institutions of higher learning, while creating greater opportunities for academic exchange and joint programmes,” he said.
Brian, who conveyed Prabowo’s greetings and best wishes to the Malaysian government and people, said these efforts would contribute to a more harmonious, prosperous, and resilient Asean, where the peoples of the region could thrive and the two nations continue to grow side by side.
“May Malaysia continue to prosper and flourish in unity, and may our two nations grow even closer in the years to come,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysia won’t be transit point for shipments supporting Israel’s military, suspicious cargo will be inspected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday reaffirmed Malaysia’s firm stance against allowing the country to be used as a transit point for any cargo contributing to Israel’s military operations.
In a statement posted on his X account, Anwar stressed that Malaysia remains committed to preventing the country from being used to support military aggression or acts against innocent lives.
“Malaysia’s position is clear and unequivocal. We will not allow our country to be used as a conduit for any shipment that supports or contributes to Israel’s military capabilities and its atrocities against Palestinians and other innocent lives.
“Any suspicious shipment will be subject to inspection and investigation in accordance with Malaysian law. Where a violation is established, decisive action will be taken,” he said.
The Prime Minister’s statement was issued alongside a foreign report highlighting a new level of scrutiny over Israel-bound shipments. — Bernama

Title: Anwar calls for Malaysia-Maldives ties to deliver tangible gains in trade, tourism and digital economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia and the Maldives have ample scope to strengthen parliamentary cooperation, including through exchange visits, sharing of experiences and the Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) platform, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said that as Commonwealth member countries, Malaysia and the Maldives had ample scope to learn from each other’s experiences in strengthening institutions, enhancing governance and improving public sector capacity.
Anwar said this in a Facebook post, after receiving a courtesy call from People’s Majlis of Maldives Speaker, Abdul Raheem Abdulla, during his two-day official visit to the country.
During the visit, he also held several meetings with the Maldives leadership to expand cooperation in strategic areas, including education, defence, trade, investment, tourism, the halal industry and the digital economy.
Anwar said his meeting with Maldives Vice-President Hussain Mohamed Latheef also discussed efforts to expand cooperation in higher education, Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), professional training and human capital development.
He also held a meeting with Maldives Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam to exchange views on the positive momentum in bilateral ties.
Officials and the business communities of both countries are also encouraged to identify specific opportunities in trade and investment, tourism, the halal industry and the digital economy, so that the good relations could be translated into tangible benefits.
He said that both sides also discussed efforts to strengthen climate resilience and the sustainable development agenda, taking into account the specific challenges faced by the Maldives, as a small developing island nation.
He added that he would also continue to work with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu and the country’s government to strengthen bilateral ties.
Anwar departed for home today after concluding a two-day official visit to the Maldives at Muizzu’s invitation, marking his first visit to the Indian Ocean island republic since becoming Prime Minister in November 2022.
The Malaysian delegation also comprised Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam. — Bernama

Title: King and Queen extend Malaysia Day greetings, pray for lasting peace and unity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Their Majesties Sultan Ibrahim and Raja Zarith Sofiah, King and Queen of Malaysia, have extended Malaysia Day greetings to all Malaysians.
In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, the King and Queen also prayed that Malaysia would continue to be blessed by Allah SWT, enjoy lasting peace, and remain protected from all forms of adversity.
Sultan Ibrahim also expressed gratitude for the longstanding unity and harmony among Malaysians of different races, saying these are vital to the country’s strength and stability. — Bernama

Title: AGC: Dropping four charges against Muhyiddin based on evidence, litigation risks; three Jana Wibawa charges remain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) stressed that the decision not to proceed with the four charges against Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin in relation to Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd was made based on a professional assessment of the evidence, the evidential viability of the case and the overall interests of the prosecution.
The AGC said the decision did not mean that the charges had been brought without basis and should not be interpreted as a finding that the transactions which were the subject of the investigation did not take place.
It said that prosecutorial decisions could and should be reviewed when the entirety of the evidence, its admissibility, the credibility of witnesses and the implications for other proceedings were assessed comprehensively, and that such decisions must be made based on the law, evidence and the interests of the administration of justice.
“The assessment showed that proceeding with the charges posed a real risk of litigation, including the risk of undermining the strategy and evidential basis of other charges still faced by the accused,” the AGC said in a statement last night.
“In such circumstances, the prosecution must consider the overall interests of the case rather than defend one charge in isolation,” it said.
The AGC also stressed that the duty of the prosecution was not to defend a particular charge at all costs, but to ensure that only charges supported by sufficient evidence and capable of being defended in court were pursued.
“After taking into account all these factors, AGC is of the view that proceeding with the charges is no longer an appropriate and prudent prosecutorial step.
“However, the prosecution involving three other predicate charges under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) against the accused will continue,” it said.
High Court Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin today discharged and acquitted Muhyiddin of one charge of using his position to obtain RM200 million in bribes and three money laundering charges involving the same amount after the prosecution informed the court that it would not proceed with the case against the Pagoh Member of Parliament in relation to Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd.
Muhyiddin, 79, is now being tried on three charges of using his position to obtain RM25.3 million in bribes for Bersatu from three companies, namely Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Mamfor Sdn Bhd and KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, as well as Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, in connection with the Jana Wibawa project.
The prosecution in Muhyiddin’s trial closed its case today after calling 29 prosecution witnesses. — Bernama

Title: Celebrating 63 years of togetherness: East Malaysians share what it means to be Malaysian
Article:
KOTA KINABALU/KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Julia Chan and Arif Zikri spoke to Sabahans and Sarawakians on what Malaysia means to them and what it means to be Malaysian.
The Sabah perspective
Ask Sabahans about being Malaysian and they can begin with something as uncomplicated and universal as good food and world class sunsets and end with something much more complicated: how to belong to a diverse federation without losing the unique identity that comes with being Sabahan.
Ahead of Malaysia Day,
Malay Mail
asked several Sabahans what comes to mind when they hear “Malaysia”, what being Malaysian means to them, how that identity differs in Sabah, and what they wish people in Peninsular Malaysia understood about being Sabahan.
What comes to mind when you hear “Malaysia”?
For many, including marine biologist Malinda Auluck, 40, the answer was first and foremost food — and the strong opinions that come with it.
“We are snobbish about our food. Want to cause an uproar? Ask for crispy skin
rendang
,” she said.
Comedian and trivia host Matt Brian, 29, had a more unexpected first thought.
“To be honest, as a comedian, the first thing I thought of was the missing plane,” he said.
Most waxed lyrical about Malaysia’s delectable food and cultural diversity although corruption was another answer, albeit one given in jest.
But jokes aside, Malaysia meant home and Sabahans loved the country’s diversity and the ability of people from different races and cultures to live alongside one another, mostly in peace.
“It’s far from perfect, but I can say it’s got the best food in the world, it’s got the best sunsets in the world, and the best people. That works for me,” Matt said.
For digital marketer Leon Kuan, 33, Malaysia brought to mind food, cultural diversity, multiple languages and the Malaysia Agreement 1963, which paved the way for the formation of the federation.
Leon, 33, feels Sabah is still misunderstood by West Malaysians and needs to be given the same respect within the Federation. — Picture by Julia Chan
What does being Malaysian mean to you?
For the Sabahans interviewed, being Malaysian was closely tied to the experience of growing up surrounded by different cultures, languages and traditions so deeply integrated into daily life that navigating them requires little conscious thought.
“The ability to move comfortably between different cultures, languages and traditions is not something I consciously practise because it has become second nature,” said Malinda.
For psychiatrist Liang Yoong, 33, being Malaysian meant being born and raised in the country while identifying with its many cultures, cuisines and languages through shared experiences.
For entrepreneur Dinoza Mahruf, 51, diversity was what made Malaysia distinctive.
“For me, being Malaysian means being proud to call home a country where diversity is our identity and unity is our strength,” he said.
Sandra, 50, says being Sabahan was part of her identity and is proud of her Sabahan roots. — Picture courtesy of Sandra Sokial
Civil servant Sandra Sokial, 50, described it as being part of “a bigger family” while remaining proud of where she came from.
“I believe that being Malaysian should not mean having to set aside my Sabahan identity,” she said.
Other answers included Malaysia’s strong passport, its affordability relative to the standard of living, government subsidies and assistance, and the warm hospitality associated with Malaysians.
Does being Malaysian mean something different in Sabah?
For the Sabahans interviewed, the answer was broadly yes — but not because they felt less Malaysian.
Rather, they described a Malaysian identity in Sabah shaped by its particularly diverse population and a culture of accommodation between communities.
Liang said Sabah had “a special kind of understanding and acceptance” that she felt was not always found in Peninsular Malaysia.
“We accept the differences and the similarities, we readily accommodate instead of insisting on basing everything on our own race or religion,” she said.
Brian described Sabah as a more “idealistic” and relaxed society.
“We’re very, very united. We’re very chill, Sabahan amalgamation. We’re tight, and we don’t take things too seriously down here in Sabah,” he said.
He said people of different religions and backgrounds could share the same spaces without necessarily making an issue of what others ate or drank.
“We’re just living our own lives. We’re very, very chill,” he said.
Matt Brian, 29, a comedian cum trivia host, believes Sabahans are 'chill" about race relations, and don't want interference from their Peninsula Malaysian counterparts. — Picture courtesy of Matt Brian
That cultural fluidity is also evident in the way Sabahans communicate, said Rozzy Rajab, 39.
She recalled travelling to Kuala Lumpur for a company event with another native Sabahan, where the two naturally switched between Sabah Malay and Mandarin while chatting with a West Malaysian make-up artist.
The make-up artist was surprised by how naturally they moved between the two languages, which Rozzy said was common and unremarkable in Sabah.
She added that Sabah’s ethnic identities could also be difficult for outsiders to neatly categorise.
“Some Kadazans look very much like Chinese and some Chinese look very Bumiputera,” she said, pointing out that people in West Malaysia were often viewed through racial lenses.
Leon, who lived in Kuala Lumpur for several years, said the level of “halal pettiness/toleration” was very different between East and West Malaysia, although Sabah also had its own sensitivities and points of contention.
For Malinda, the Sabahan experience also meant being more conscious of inequalities within Malaysia.
“For me, the biggest difference is the sense of privilege. Growing up in Sabah, the development gap is much more visible, so you're constantly aware that access to infrastructure, education, healthcare and opportunities isn't equal for everyone.
“I don't know if someone who has only lived in big cities like Kuala Lumpur and Selangor would notice this in the same way, because many of those conveniences are simply part of everyday life there,” she said.
What is one thing you wish West Malaysians understood about being Sabahan?
The answers varied, but a common thread emerged: Sabahans do not want their identity reduced to race, religion or politics — and being proud to be Sabahan should never be interpreted as being less Malaysian.
For auditor Peter Wong, 35, it came down to “tolerance and understanding”.
“Not everything revolves around race, religion and politics,” he said.
Brian was even more direct.
“Don’t come here with your identity politics,” he said.
“Don’t try to split us up according to race, according to religion, according to political party. We don’t need that. We’re doing just fine.”
For Rozzy, one thing she wished Peninsular Malaysians understood was Sabah’s relatively easy-going relationship between different faiths and communities.
She said people in Sabah were generally accustomed to celebrating together and respecting each other’s practices without making every interaction a religious issue.
“Definitely don’t come here and cause trouble. Muslims and non Muslims in Sabah are very tolerant towards each other and non judgemental. We celebrate the festivities without issue and genuine celebrated our differences,” she said.
Malinda pointed to another big misconception — that Sabah’s lower level of development meant the cost of living was cheaper.
“In reality, many things are just as expensive, if not more expensive, than in the Peninsula. That’s something many Sabahans live with every day,” she said.
She also pointed to the high cost of travelling between Sabah and the Peninsula, particularly airfares.
Leon, meanwhile, pointed to Sabah’s constitutional position and the Malaysia Agreement 1963. He said many Sabahans struggled to be viewed as equal to their West Malaysian counterparts, whether at a personal or political level.
“When you mention Malaysia, Peninsular people will mention August 31 as National Day. But September 16, the day Malaysia was formed, is not given the same prominence,” he said.
He argued that Sabah and Sarawak should not simply be viewed in the same way as the other states in the federation, reflecting the long-running Sabah and Sarawak position on their status and rights under MA63.
Sandra similarly said Sabahans had their own history and perspective on the formation of Malaysia.
“We see ourselves not simply as another state, but as one of the partners that formed Malaysia, and that shapes how we understand our place in the federation,” she said.
“For many Sabahans, this is not about being less Malaysian. It is about being recognised as an equal partner and having our position respected.”
Dinoza’s message to Peninsular Malaysians was simpler.
“We are Malaysians too,” he said.
There was plenty of pride in Malaysia — its food, diversity, hospitality, shared languages and the ability of people from different backgrounds to live alongside one another.
But there was also a clear desire for that Malaysian identity to accommodate the particular experience of being Sabahan — one shaped by geography, development gaps, cultural fluidity and a different understanding of Malaysia’s formation.
For those interviewed, being Sabahan and being Malaysian were not competing identities.
As Sandra put it: “Being proud to be Sabahan does not make us less Malaysian.”
A strong sense of belonging
Multi-award-winning songstress Dayang Nurfaizah, born and raised in Kuching, said that Malaysia is home above all else. — Picture via Instagram
Merdeka Day honours the legacy of 1957, but Malaysia Day marks the union that completed the country.
Malay Mail sat down with several Sarawakian celebrities to explore heritage, identity, and the Bornean pride shaping modern Malaysia.
Multi-award-winning songstress Dayang Nurfaizah, born and raised in Kuching, said that Malaysia is home above all else.
“The food, the people, everything is so warm and colourful.
“Even with all our differences, somehow it all just..works,” Dayang said.
She added that for her, being a Malaysian means celebrating unity in diversity and growing up with different races, languages and cultures is something that she takes pride in.
The
Di Pintu Syurga
singer also calls for greater cultural awareness from Peninsular Malaysians, pointing out that Sarawak’s unique identity and heritage are just as central to the nation’s fabric as any state in Semenanjung.
“I wish more Semenanjung folks knew Sarawak has its own identity, its own languages and cultures.
“We’re not just ‘the other side’, we are just as Malaysian (as you are),” she said.
Sibu-born actress and Mandopop star Stella Chung proudly carries her Malaysian identity wherever she goes in the world. — Picture via Instagram
For Sibu-born actress and Mandopop star Stella Chung, celebrating Malaysia’s rich diversity doesn’t stop at home—she proudly carries her Malaysian identity wherever she goes in the world.
“To me, it’s a strong sense of belonging, and I’m really proud to be a Malaysian.
“I’ve travelled quite a bit because of work, and it actually makes me appreciate Malaysia even more.
“Whenever someone asks where I’m from, I’m always happy to say, “I’m from Malaysia!” she said.
Chung, who spent most of her childhood in the neighbouring town of Sarikei, also pointed out that Sarawak’s beauty extends beyond its beautiful scenery and delicious food – it is the warmth of its people and how cultures organically blend together that makes the state special.
“What I love most is the warmth of the people here. People from different races and cultures get along so naturally and celebrate each other’s festivals together.
“I’d really love for more people from Semenanjung to visit Sarawak and experience it for themselves — I’m sure you’ll love it here!” Chung said.
Iban singer and news presenter Melissa Francis believes that Malaysia’s cultural acceptance is rooted in fundamental values like mutual respect and good manners. — Picture via Instagram
However, popular Iban singer and news presenter Melissa Francis believes that Malaysia’s cultural acceptance is rooted in fundamental values like mutual respect and good manners.
The
Sulu Mata Engkudu
singer from Sri Aman pointed out that one of her favourite things about Sarawak is how people from different races and religions could coexist harmoniously and even eat together at the same table regardless of having different dietary requirements.
“Let’s appreciate the things we have now which are peace, prosperity and harmony and let's educate our children and the younger generations by sharing with them what makes us great – which is having mutual respect for each other’s religions and races.
“If we truly want a ‘happily ever after’ for Malaysia, stop fighting with each other, especially toying around with sensitive issues such as religion.
“I believe that if we take care of our manners and show respect to each other, none of this (the fighting) would happen,” Francis told
Malay Mail.
Muhammad Radhi Razali, the frontman of famous rock band OAG who is also from Kuching, he wished that more Malaysians would acknowledge or show their appreciation towards Sabah and Sarawak who also fought hard for independence. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Meanwhile, for Muhammad Radhi Razali, the frontman of famous rock band OAG who is also from Kuching, he wished that more Malaysians would acknowledge or show their appreciation towards Sabah and Sarawak who also fought hard for independence.
“I wish the Semenanjung know that we also fought hard and smart against the colonisers in order to gain Merdeka.
“And we are humbly proud of being Malaysian,” Radhi said.
When asked what the word ‘Malaysia’ means to him, Radhi simply offered “Boleh!”—invoking the iconic national slogan—before closing with the enduring words of Iban warrior Rentap: “
Agi Idup Agi Ngelaban
” (“As long as you live, keep fighting”).

Title: MACC officer retracts police report against Muhyiddin’s lawyer; court decides not to cite for contempt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today decided not to begin contempt of court proceedings against Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation officer Mazery Mohd Zaini, as it accepted the officer’s explanations about his MACC colleague’s police report.
Earlier today, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyers had accused Mazery of contempt of court, due to his actions that led to the police report.
Muhyiddin’s lawyers had pointed out that Mazery was still testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s trial, and should not have communicated with anyone including the MACC colleague who lodged the police report.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin this afternoon delivered her decision on whether to start contempt of court proceedings against Mazery.
The judge noted that she had told all prosecution witnesses in this trial to not discuss matters in this trial with anyone, while they remain on the witness stand.
“But just now, his explanation is that he wants to check that there is no information leak from MACC itself. So it can be said that this witness is overly-cautious and I accept his explanation. I think I will not proceed to cite for contempt.
“But Datuk Amer, it’s entirely up to you if you want to take further legal action, I don’t want to comment on that. But for the court, I accept his explanation,” the judge said towards the end of today’s court proceedings, referring to Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad.
Mazery had testified yesterday and was supposed to continue testifying today, while the police report was lodged by his MACC colleague last night.
Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex on September 2, 2026. Picture by Firdaus Latif
What the police report is about and what happened to it
This morning, Amer highlighted the police report, which he described as a form of “intimidation” against Muhyiddin’s lawyers and an “underhanded tactic” to undermine the trial.
The police report had named Amer as having presented to the court an allegedly classified document, namely Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad’s statement to MACC during investigations.
Amer said however that Muhyiddin’s lawyers did not obtain the document from MACC or through illegal or improper methods, stressing that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had obtained it from Adam Radlan’s lawyers.
Amer said he reserved his rights to take legal action against Mazery, while the latter apologised to Muhyiddin’s lawyers and said he did not intend to tarnish their reputation.
Mazery explained that the police report was lodged to protect MACC’s integrity, as he was worried that Adam Radlan’s statement had been leaked from MACC despite being a classified document.
This afternoon, Mazery returned to the High Court after confirming that there had been no information leaks.
Mazery also confirmed that the police report had been given a “No Further Action” (NFA) status, and a fresh police report had been lodged to withdraw last night’s police report.
“As a result of investigations which I carried out at the headquarters, it was found that there are no information leaks from MACC officers, and I am satisfied that no evidence or documents came from MACC officers,” he told the High Court, saying that last night’s police report had been retracted and has been given “NFA” status.
Mazery also expressed hope that Amer could accept his apology.
KUALAL LUMPUR 16/2/2024 Segambut Bersatu Division Deputy Chief Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad was seen here at Kuala Lumpur Court Complex. PICTURE BY SAYUTI ZAINUDIN
What Mazery told Muhyiddin’s lawyer
After Mazery’s update on the withdrawal of the police report, he was cross-examined by Amer.
Mazery said he had yesterday instructed his subordinate to lodge a police report to determine whether Adam Radlan’s statement had been leaked, but confirmed that this subordinate was not present in court yesterday and would not know what happened in court.
Mazery confirmed that he did not make any checks on whether the document had been leaked before the police report was lodged last night, and confirmed that his checks today with another MACC colleague on whether there had been leaks only took between 15 to 20 minutes.
Mazery confimed he did not contact this MACC colleague yesterday, but disagreed he could have done so before the police report was lodged.
While confirming that he had decided to lodge the police report without first carrying out an internal investigation and without clarifying with Muhyiddin’s lawyers, Mazery denied that the police report was a “deliberate plan” by him to prevent Muhyiddin’s lawyers from asking four recalled prosecution witnesses today about Adam Radlan.
Mazery confirmed that only he and his subordinate had received a copy of last night’s police report, and denied leaking it to a news outlet which had this morning published a news report on the police report.
Among other things, Mazery denied that he wanted to suppress facts that are in favour of Muhyiddin in this case, also disagreeing that the police report was lodged and leaked to the media to deter Amer from pursuing issues linked to Adam Radlan.
Later when asked by lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin to clarify why the initial police report was lodged, Mazery stressed it was purely to check if Adam Radlan’s statement had been leaked by MACC officers.
“So when there is none, I was satisfied that there is none, there is no need to continue with that report, that’s why I made an immediate retraction,” he said, adding that he has no malicious intention and that he had cooperated with both the prosecution and Muhyiddin from the start of investigations until now.
Before the judge delivered her decision on whether to cite Mazery for contempt, Wan Shaharuddin also addressed the police report incident in court.
“As the lead prosecutor in this case, I take responsibility for what had happened today. I myself apologise to Datuk Amer on this incident,” Wan Shaharuddin said, before closing the prosecution’s case in the trial after calling in 29 witnesses over more than 30 days of hearing.
When the trial resumes on November 26 and December 1 to 3, the prosecution and Muhyiddin’s lawyers are expected to present their arguments on whether Muhyiddin will have to enter his defence in this case.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is now facing only three charges of power abuse involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd).

Title: Ringgit slides against euro, yen and pound as greenback gains momentum
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The ringgit ended lower against the US dollar on Tuesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the two-day US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which begins tonight, an analyst said.
At 6pm, the local currency dipped to 4.0835/0880 against the greenback from Monday’s close of 4.0735/0770.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the odds for a US rate hike this week were reportedly at 92.3 per cent based on data from CME FedWatch. CME FedWatch is a tool by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME Group) that shows market expectations for the US Federal Reserve’s (Fed) interest-rate decisions.
“Consequently, the US Dollar Index (DXY) rose 0.25 per cent to 99.641 points while the 10-year US Treasury note yield surpassed the 5.00 per cent level. Other Asian currencies such as the Indonesian rupiah, Thai baht and Singapore dollar were also weaker against the US dollar,” he told Bernama today.
At the close, the ringgit weakened against the euro to 4.7111/7163 from Monday’s close of 4.7008/7049, fell against yen to 2.6366/6396 from 2.6355/6380, and inched down vis-a-vis the British pound to 5.5037/5098 from 5.4931/4978 previously.
Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit eased against the Singapore dollar to 3.2093/2131 from 3.2055/2085, and retreated against the Thai baht to 12.2620/2800 from 12.2445/2598.
The local note was also marginally lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 230.7/231.1 from 230.5/230.8 yesterday, and was down vis-à-vis the Philippine peso to 6.50/6.51 from 6.48/6.49 previously. — Bernama

Title: SWCorp: Investigation papers on construction waste dumping from Singapore to be ready in three months
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 15 – The Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) is currently finalising four investigation papers on the dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian.
Johor SWCorp director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said that the investigation papers are expected to be completed in three months time before being referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor for further action.
“The probe involves four parcels of land in the affected areas and the statements of two landowners have been recorded.
“We will obtain statements from the remaining two to complete the investigation papers,” he told reporters after inspecting the community service order involving 26 offenders at De Stulang here today.
Zainal Fitri was commenting on SWCorp’s investigation progress into the alleged dumping of construction waste from Singapore in Pontian.
He added that monitoring by his SWCorp showed that there were no new cases of illegal dumping of waste from abroad in other areas.
“So far, there are no new cases reported and investigations will continue for the purpose of prosecution on the existing cases,” he said.
Previously, Pontian district officer Mohd Farid Hassan was reported saying that the locations identified as dumping sites for the construction waste included Kampung Sungai Karang, Kampung Sungai Senai, and Kampung Simpang Kiri.
Johor Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said that a special committee — comprising the local authorities, police, district office and SWCorp — have conducted a comprehensive investigation into the issue.
On the community service order, Zainal Fitri said that the latest session involved 12 locals, while the remaining 14 were non-citizens, comprising seven Bangladeshis, three Nepalis, three Indonesians, and one Pakistani.
He said the cases involved minor littering offences in public areas, comprising 25 instances of discarding cigarette butts and one instance of discarding a beverage can.
“This community service order is part of an enforcement approach via legal channels that not only has a rehabilitative effect on offenders but also aims to educate the public on the importance of maintaining public cleanliness.
“It’s  implementation is not merely a punishment, but a direct civic education approach for offenders to understand the impact of irresponsible littering and to foster awareness on maintaining environmental cleanliness,” he said.

Title: Kelana Jaya line operations back on track after morning signal fault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Rapid KL’s Kelana Jaya Line, which was disrupted by a signalling fault this morning, has returned to normal operations and is running according to schedule.
Rapid KL, in a statement today, said that the disruption, detected at 9.14 am at Ampang Park Station, caused a train to stop with its doors not aligned with the platform screen doors, affecting the smooth movement of passengers.
Following the incident, its operations and technical teams took immediate action to restore the affected system and conducted continuous monitoring to ensure operations returned to normal as soon as possible.
“Following the action taken, operations on the Kelana Jaya Line have returned to normal, and all trains are operating according to schedule,” it said.
The company is now closely monitoring the signalling system involved to ensure the service continues to operate smoothly and at an optimal level.
Rapid KL also apologised for any inconvenience caused to passengers by the incident. — Bernama

Title: Haze: 39 areas hit unhealthy API levels as of 4pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — A total of 39 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy air quality, with Johan Setia recording the highest reading at 188, followed by Shah Alam (173), Klang (167), Petaling Jaya (166), Banting (164) and Kuala Selangor (163).
Two areas in Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Serian (171) and Samarahan (151).
In Johor, seven areas recorded unhealthy API levels, namely Tangkak (172), Pasir Gudang (167), Kota Tinggi (164), Larkin (161), Batu Pahat (160), Pengerang (160) and Segamat (117).
Pahang recorded five areas with unhealthy air quality, involving Indera Mahkota Kuantan (167), Temerloh (163), Jerantut (163), Balok Baru Kuantan (162) and Rompin (154).
In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy readings - Nilai (176), Seremban (172) and Port Dickson (159).
In Terengganu, the affected areas were Kemaman (161), Paka (158) and Kuala Terengganu (157), while in Perak they were Tanjung Malim (166), Seri Manjung (160), Tasek Ipoh (157) and Pagoh Ipoh (104)
Two areas in Melaka - Alor Gajah and Bukit Rambai, recorded unhealthy readings at 164 each, while in Penang, unhealthy levels were recorded in Balik Pulau (154), Minden (152) and Seberang Jaya (139).

Meanwhile, 29 areas nationwide recorded moderate API levels.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 301 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin relieved after acquittal on four charges, hopes to be freed from three remaining charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin today expressed relief after the High Court decided to acquit him on four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd.
Thanking his lawyers and also expressing gratitude to Allah on his acquittal, Muhyiddin said: “And Alhamdulillah, that decision is a decision that I really welcome, feel relieved as from the start I am of the view that I am innocent.
“So thank you to all who have prayed for my acquittal today,” he told reporters when met at the court complex here.
Muhyiddin expressed hope that he would also be freed of the remaining three charges that he is still facing in this trial.
“Praylah, hopefully the remaining charges that are still outstanding, which today have completed trial, soon there will be submissions in court, and I hope that I am also freed from the other remaining charges,” he said.
Earlier today, the prosecution applied to the High Court to temporarily release Muhyiddin from four of the seven charges in this trial after evaluating the case as a whole, and applied for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on just the four charges.
Muhyiddin’s lawyers had urged for Muhyiddin to be acquitted on those four charges instead.
After considering arguments from both sides, the High Court decided that Muhyiddin should be acquitted instead of merely given a DNAA for those four charges.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin said this was because the prosecution did not give any reasons besides saying it did not wish to proceed with the four charges, and that the prosecution had left it to the court to decide.
“I’m of the view in the interests of justice, the discretion of the court is to be exercised in favour of the accused,” the judge said.
“So with that, the court discharges and acquits the accused from those four charges only. And we will continue with this case, with the three remaining charges related to Jana Wibawa,” the judge had said.
This afternoon, the prosecution closed its case on the three charges after calling in 29 prosecution witnesses over more than 30 days of hearing.
The High Court has scheduled November 26, December 1 to 3 to hear submissions from the prosecution and Muhyiddin’s lawyers on whether the former PM will have to defend himself in this case.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is now facing only three charges of power abuse involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd).
