Title: Lawyer Haniff Khatri says decades of legal notes and 28 years of memories lost in Country Homes house fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Three decades of handwritten journals, irreplaceable legal notes, and 28 years of family memories were reduced to ash early today after a devastating fire gutted the home of prominent lawyer Mohamed Haniff Khatri Abdulla in Bandar Country Homes.
The blaze, which broke out around 3am, completely consumed the upper floor of the residence, incinerating beds, clothing, home appliances, and personal archives that Haniff had accumulated over more than 30 years of legal practice,
NST
reported.
Among the charred debris lay fragments of book pages and ruined family mementos. His son, Mohamed Hamzah Khatri Mohamed Haniff, sifted through the wreckage to find a handheld gaming console on his bedroom floor, one of the few items to survive the flames.
“My graduation photos were in my room when the fire happened,” Hamzah said, hoping his university portraits might still somehow be salvaged.
The family was also left searching for their pets, with two recently adopted kittens believed to have been inside his sister’s room when the fire erupted, leaving behind only an empty carrier and a packet of cat food near the entrance.
Haniff had lived in the residence with his family since 1998, raising his children under its roof for nearly three decades.
“So we have stayed here for 28 years. My daughter, the eldest one, was two and a half years old when we moved here,” he said.
The incident unfolded while Haniff was downstairs watching a football match. His daughter discovered the fire in the first-floor living room after stepping out of her bedroom for a drink of water and screamed for help.
Haniff grabbed half a pail of water and raced upstairs to battle the flames, but was rapidly forced back by the blinding smoke and blistering heat.
“The fumes were already in my mouth, were already in my throat.
“It was so hot, I felt a bit of a burn,” he said.
The family of four fled into the street as household items exploded and glass windows shattered around them. Firefighters arrived within 10 minutes to bring the blaze under control and treated Haniff for a minor burn sustained during the escape.
“They (the Fire and Rescue Department) came with their own first-aid kit. When I realised there was a bit of burn... they helped me,” he said.
Despite the near-total destruction of their possessions, father and son chose gratitude over despair.
“At least everyone is safe. That’s the most important thing.
“These items, it’s all secondary. Life is more important,” Hamzah said.
Haniff affirmed that the family has embraced spiritual acceptance: “As Muslims, we have to redha.”

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB insists has no unilateral power over Yang Di-Pertuan Besar, but stays silent on alleged proclamation signing
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 15 — Negeri Sembilan Mentri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim insisted today that he has no unilateral power over the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir, but stopped short of confirming or denying that he signed a disputed document at the centre of a growing constitutional row.
The state executive council, which Ismail chairs, said in a statement that questions over the so-called Instrument of Proclamation must be resolved strictly under the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 (UUTKNS) and the principle of constitutional monarchy, "not as a political or personal matter."
The statement comes after the Undang Yang Empat — the state's four ruling chiefs — and other traditional leaders publicly alleged that Ismail signed a proclamation on August 3effecting the dethronement of Tuanku Muhriz.
According to the Undang, the document was signed at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on the same day Ismail was received in audience and installed as mentri besar. Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, who identifies himself as Undang Luak Jelebu, has since produced what he says is a copy of the instrument bearing Ismail's signature, dated August 3 and invoking Article 10(2) of the UUTKNS.
Ismail has separately lodged a police report over the matter and has publicly reaffirmed his loyalty to Tuanku Muhriz as the reigning Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
He has also avoided journalists' questions on the episode, including after a closed-door meeting last week with Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who had sought a personal explanation from him over claims he was forced to sign the document.
His statement today did not address either the police report or the disputed document directly.
Instead, it laid out a five-point legal framework arguing that a proclamation "does not by itself create constitutional power," that the MB's involvement in any process under the UUTKNS does not amount to a power to determine the Ruler's position on his own, and that the matter should ultimately be settled through "judicial determination" if a legal dispute arises.
“In a system of Constitutional Monarchy, power must derive from the Constitution and the law,” the statement said.
“The Royal Institution, the Undang, the mentri besar, and the state government each hold a position and function determined by the Constitution.”
The dispute has already drawn in Umno's national leadership and threatens to overshadow the early weeks of Ismail's administration, which took office on August 2 following the Barisan Nasional–Perikatan Nasional coalition's state election win.
No date has been set for any court proceedings, and neither the palace nor the Undang Yang Empat have issued a formal response to Tuesday's statement.

Title: Malaysia agrees in principle to support Maldives’ US$100m soft loan request, says Anwar
Article:
MALE, Sept 15 — Malaysia has agreed in principle to support the Maldives’ application for a US$100 million (US$1=RM4.07) financing facility, which Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described as a form of soft loan to be implemented through both countries’ monetary authorities.
Anwar said that the terms and mechanism for the facility are still being worked out by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA).
He said that in principle, Malaysia has no issue with the application, taking into account the Maldives’ repayment record and the cooperation between the two countries, as well as the government guarantee that would need to be provided.
“It is essentially a soft loan, but it will be carried out through Bank Negara and the financial authorities.
“As for the terms, these are still being examined by both central banks, although in principle we have no issue with their repayment record, as well as the cooperation and government guarantee that must be in place,” he told the Malaysian media after concluding his official visit to the country.
Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.
Earlier, at a joint press conference with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, Anwar said the Maldivian leader had raised the matter with him and had also written regarding the need for BNM to respond to the MMA’s request for the US$100 million facility.
“The President has written to me about the need to get our central bank, Bank Negara Malaysia, to respond to the Maldivian request, precisely (from) the Maldives Monetary Authority, for this US$100 million facility.
“We have agreed in principle to support this, although both the central bank and MMA will have to work in the fastest time possible on the mechanism and the process to ensure that the agreement can be settled in the fastest time possible. And this can only be done based on trust and friendship,” he said.
The Prime Minister is on a two-day official visit to the Maldives and held a four-eye meeting and bilateral talks with Muizzu today. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Malaysia, Maldives to expand cooperation in maritime security, halal and haj
Article:
MALE, Sept 15 — Malaysia and the Maldives are set to expand cooperation in maritime security and training, as well as halal, wakaf and haj, following the exchange of two memoranda of understanding (MoUs) on defence and Islamic affairs today.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that as a maritime nation, the Maldives placed particular importance on maritime cooperation, including security and training.
“The Maldives is a maritime nation and places great importance on maritime cooperation, as well as cooperation in security, training and maritime safety and security, which we will continue to pursue,” he told Malaysian media after completing his official programme at the President’s Office here today.
On Islamic affairs, Anwar said the Maldives’ status as an Islamic country provided opportunities to deepen cooperation in areas including halal, dakwah, Muslim affairs, waqf and haj.
Earlier, Anwar and Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu witnessed the exchange of the two cooperation documents at the President’s Office.
At a joint press conference later, Muizzu said the agreements opened new avenues for practical cooperation while strengthening the institutional foundations of Malaysia-Maldives bilateral relations.
“Today we witnessed the exchange of new cooperation agreements in two important areas, which are defence cooperation and Islamic faith.
“These agreements open new avenues for practical cooperation and further strengthen the institutional foundations of our bilateral relationship,” he said.
Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Johari Abdul Ghani, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Malaysian High Commissioner to Sri Lanka and the Maldives Badli Hisham Adam.
Anwar is on a two-day official visit to the Maldives, which ends this afternoon. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin trial: Prosecution completes case after 29 witnesses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The prosecution today completed its case in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin's power abuse trial after calling in 29 prosecution witnesses, which means that the trial will now move on to the next stage.
Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin this afternoon told the High Court that the prosecution closes its case, and that the prosecution will offer six witnesses that Muhyiddin could call in as his witnesses if he is ordered to defend himself in this case.
"With that, the prosecution closes this case. I offer the following witnesses," he said, while listing the potential witnesses and promising to help call in those witnesses if required by Muhyiddin.
The six are Muhyiddin's then deputy chief private secretary Asmar Asmadi Abdullah Sani, Muhyiddin's former principal private secretary Datuk Marzuki Mohamad, Datuk Mohd Ayob Mohd Ali, former Treasury secretary-general Datuk Seri Asri Hamidon, Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer Mohd Syahmeizy Sulong, and Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin then scheduled four days for continued hearing, namely November 26, December 1 to 3.
When the trial resumes in November and December, the prosecution and Muhyiddin's lawyers are expected to present their arguments on whether Muhyiddin will have to enter his defence in this case.
There are two stages in a criminal trial, with the prosecution having to prove that it has shown a prima facie case after calling in all the prosecution witnesses.
After hearing the arguments from both sides, the High Court will decide whether there is a prima facie case.
If the High Court finds there is no prima facie case, Muhyiddin would be acquitted.
If the High Court decides there is a prima facie case, the trial would move on to the defence stage where Muhyiddin would be ordered to defend himself.
Muhyiddin's trial started on March 9, and has gone on for about 32 days now.
Earlier today, the prosecution applied for a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA) for four of the seven charges that Muhyiddin is facing in this trial, with the High Court then exercising its discretion under the law to acquit Muhyiddin on the four charges in the interests of justice.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is now facing only three charges of power abuse involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd).

Title: Four of seven missing anglers found safe off Sekinchan, search continues for three
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 15 — Four of the seven anglers reported missing yesterday were found safe by a local fishing boat in the waters off Sekinchan, 25 nautical miles from the coast of Sungai Besar, at about 9.50 am today.
Selangor Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) director Abdul Muhaimin Muhammad Salleh said the four men were found floating close to one another and were in a weak condition.
“They are now receiving treatment at Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR), Klang, and Banting Hospital, Kuala Langat, while the cause of the incident is still under investigation.
“Hazy conditions reduced visibility and made the SAR operation slightly more challenging,” he said in a statement.
He said the search and rescue operation was ongoing to locate the remaining three victims, with the maritime search area expanded to 203.5 square nautical miles, while the aerial search covers 764 square nautical miles.
He said the second day of the SAR operation involved MMEA sea and air assets, as well as assets from the Royal Malaysia Police, Fire and Rescue Department, Civil Defence Force and two local fishing boats.
“MMEA will continue to coordinate the search efforts with the agencies involved to ensure the SAR operation is carried out comprehensively and continuously until all the victims are located.
“Any information related to the incident can be channelled to Selangor MMEA at 013-660 6652,” he added.
Six anglers and a boat skipper were reported missing after they could not be located in the waters off One Fathom Bank, near Pulau Ketam. — Bernama

Title: Babysitter pleads not guilty to exposing toddler to conditions that could have caused death
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — A babysitter pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of exposing a 13-month-old boy under her care to conditions that could have caused his death last week.
Noraidah Khairuddin, 44, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Irwan Suainbon.
According to the charge, Noraidah, as a person having custody of the toddler, was accused of exposing him in a manner that could have caused his death.
“I plead not guilty because I did not do anything to him,” she said.
The offence was allegedly committed at a house in Taman Desa Mawar, Lintang Kampung Melayu 2, Air Itam, at 2 pm on Sept 8.
She was charged under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which provides for a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor M Darrshini offered bail of RM20,000 with one surety, along with conditions that the accused report to a nearby police station on the first of every month and refrain from tampering with the prosecution witnesses.
The accused’s lawyer, Naqieya Zulkernain of the National Legal Aid Foundation, sought a reduction in bail on the grounds that her client is a housewife who depends on her husband, who has no fixed income, and that they have three children.
The court granted bail of RM8,000 with one surety, along with the additional conditions requested by the prosecution and fixed case mention for Nov 16, pending the post-mortem report.
On Sept 10, police detained Noraidah and the boy’s mother to assist investigations after he was found unconscious with bluish lips at the babysitter’s home in Air Itam. — Bernama

Title: KL police propose KK Mart stores as safety points to boost crime prevention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The Kuala Lumpur Police propose making KK Mart convenience stores as Go-To-Safety-Point (GTSP) locations through a strategic collaboration with the company to strengthen crime monitoring and prevention efforts in the capital.
Its chief, Datuk Fadil Marsus said his team has identified around 700 KK Mart branches in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor that operate 24 hours, have bright lighting, and are equipped with centralised closed-circuit television (CCTV) systems, which have the potential to be safe locations for the public to seek assistance during emergencies.
“We see that KK Mart can be made a safety point for the surrounding community. At the same time, we will enhance cooperation in terms of patrolling and monitoring so that these premises become safe places for the public,” he said.
He said this to reporters at the press conference for the opening of the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent headquarters (IPK) today, which was also attended by KK Supermart & Superstore Sdn Bhd founder and executive chairman Datuk Seri Dr Chai Kee Kan.
Fadil said that they are also looking into the possibility of being granted access to the centralised CCTV of the convenience store chain, which simultaneously strengthens security monitoring in the surrounding area.
According to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the GTSP programme is an initiative that creates a network of strategic partner premises as safety points for the public to obtain immediate assistance in the event of an emergency, a crime, or a security threat.
Meanwhile, Fadil said that the KK Mart branch at the Kuala Lumpur IPK is the first convenience store branch in the PDRM building. and there may be more opened in PDRM buildings that will benefit the police personnel and the local community.
Commenting on the control of goods sold at the KK Mart premises in the Kuala Lumpur IPK, he said that the business operations are subject to government premises regulations, and any prohibited goods will not be allowed for sale.
Meanwhile, Chai said that there are currently around 1,100 KK Mart branches nationwide, and he sees great potential to place the convenience store in government buildings.
He also welcomed KK Mart’s initiative as a GTSP and was willing to share CCTV footage from the convenience store chain to assist PDRM investigations. —Bernama

Title: Anwar moots Malaysia-Maldives joint commission in KL this year
Article:
MALÉ, Sept 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed convening the Malaysia-Maldives Joint Commission in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year to further advance bilateral relations between the two countries.
Anwar said the Commission would be an important platform to address outstanding issues and translate the close relationship between Malaysia and the Maldives into concrete cooperation.
He said bilateral ties must be built on a sincere appreciation of each other’s needs and strengths, underpinned by mutual respect and trust at both the leadership and country-to-country levels.
“That is why, when the President showed such fondness and commitment, I then proposed that the Joint Commission between the two countries be facilitated at the earliest possible time.
“We will host it in Kuala Lumpur before the end of this year. And that will showcase our commitment to enhance bilateral relations between our two brotherly and sisterly countries,” he said this at a joint press conference with Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu at the President’s Office here today.
Anwar said the Commission could also address issues affecting Maldivians in Malaysia, including students and those seeking healthcare.
More than 2,000 Maldivian students were studying in Malaysia, reflecting not only the friendship between the two countries but also Maldivians’ confidence in Malaysia’s education system, he noted.
He said there were some bureaucratic issues involving parents accompanying their children studying in Malaysia, which he had discussed with his colleagues and hoped could be addressed at the next Cabinet meeting.
“I don’t think this is an issue of policy differences. We don’t have problems with Maldivians living in Malaysia, working in Malaysia, or even studying in Malaysia. So I think we will showcase this and respond positively,” the Prime Minister said.
On healthcare, Anwar said issues involving a small number of Maldivians requiring assistance should be resolved promptly, in keeping with the compassion and caring values underpinning the MADANI framework. — Bernama

Title: Don’t rush: Home minister urges Malaysians to avoid MyKad replacement frenzy
Article:
PORT DICKSON, Sept 15 — The people have been advised not to rush to replace their MyKad when applications for the new version open on Sept 17, to avoid congestion at National Registration Department (NRD) offices.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the replacement exercise for the new MyKad, which comes with about 50 additional security features, would be carried out in phases, while existing cards would remain valid for daily transactions.
“I would like to advise people not to rush to replace their MyKad. There are currently 24 million MyKad cards in circulation, with an average of 180,000 to 200,000 cards issued each month,” he told reporters here today.
He said the replacement of the MyKad would not affect subsidy balances or eligibility for subsidies linked to the identity card.
“There is no issue regarding the subsidy balance...the records are based on the existing MyKad,” he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said the department handles between 13,000 and 15,000 cases of unregistered births each year, a figure he described as still high even though Malaysia gained independence decades ago.
He said failure to register births was due to various factors, including lack of information, social problems and family issues, which could ultimately affect the children’s future.
“The reality is that there are still people who lack the basic knowledge that every birth must be registered, and this is still regarded as something normal,” he said, adding that parents or guardians gave various reasons for failing to register their children’s births, including financial difficulties and family constraints, even though birth registration is free.
In this regard, he urged parents, guardians and members of the public with information on unregistered births to come forward to NRD offices for assistance. — Bernama

Title: Prosecution drops four charges against Muhyiddin, presses on with three in corruption trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — The High Court today acquitted former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin of four charges involving Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd's funds, as the prosecution today said it does not want to proceed with trial on those charges for now.
In this trial, Muhyiddin faced seven charges:
four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and
three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
Following the High Court's decision after the prosecution's request for a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA), Muhyiddin now only faces three power abuse charges involving RM25.3 million in alleged bribes for his party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in relation to Jana Wibawa projects.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin delivered her decision this afternoon on whether to only grant a DNAA or to acquit Muhyiddin on those four charges.
Ultimately, the judge decided to acquit, in the interests of justice.
The judge noted that the prosecution did not give any reasons besides saying it did not wish to proceed with the four charges, and that the prosecution had left it to the court to decide.
“I’m of the view in the interests of justice, the discretion of the court is to be exercised in favour of the accused.
“So with that, the court discharges and acquits the accused from those four charges only. And we will continue with this case, with the three remaining charges related to Jana Wibawa,” the judge said.
Just before lunch break today, deputy public prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib informed the High Court that the prosecution had decided to not continue with four of the seven charges in Muhyiddin's trial, saying this was after the prosecution had looked at the case as a whole.
"With that, the prosecution respectfully applies for Section 254(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code to be applied, to apply for an order from this court for a DNAA on the accused. We apply for DNAA only on those charges," he said.
Muhyiddin's lawyers had however urged the High Court to acquit Muhyiddin on the four charges related to Bukhary Equity, instead of only granting a DNAA.
KUALA LUMPUR 10/03/2026 Lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik was seen at the compound during former prime miniser Tan Sri Muhyiddn Yassin’s corruption case here at Kuala Lumpur Court Complex. PICTURE BY SAYUTI ZAINUDIN
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik argued that it was clear and obvious that the prosecution was “no longer interested” in proceeding with the four charges, and also said the prosecution did not give strong reasons for why the court should give a DNAA instead of an acquittal.
“The law is very clear. Strong reasons must be given, otherwise the court has no choice but to grant a discharge amounting to an acquittal,” he argued.
“This morning, very clear, the prosecution has not provided any reasons as to why the accused cannot be acquitted and discharged.
“Unless we have good grounds given by the prosecution, exceptional grounds, cogent grounds as to why they cannot proceed, the accused must be entitled to an order of discharge amounting to acquittal (DAA). The accused person needs to move on, he’s got his public life and private life to manage.
“And under the circumstances and in the name of justice and fairness, it’s not fair for the sword of the prosecution to hang over his head for an indefinite time,” Hisyam said, urging the court to acquit Muhyiddin on the four charges “in the name of fairness and justice”.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Chetan Jethwani also argued that there is “real world prejudice” if Muhyiddin is not acquitted of the four charges, claiming that the prosecution had been relying on the four charges in order to freeze and seize Muhyiddin’s party Bersatu’s accounts for the last three years.
Chetan said a court challenge against the authorities’ freezing and seizure of Bersatu’s funds is currently still pending at the Court of Appeal.
KUALA LUMPUR 02/03/2023 Deputy Public Prosecutor Ahmad Akram Gharib was seen at the compound during the 1 Malaysia Developement Berhad (1MDB) here at Kuala Lumpur Court Complex. PICTURE BY SAYUTI ZAINUDIN
In response, Akram said the prosecution was not saying that the four charges against Muhyiddin were “wrong”, but said it is merely using its discretionary powers under Section 254(1) of the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC) to not continue with these charges.
While reiterating that the prosecution’s DNAA application for the four charges was after it had evaluated the entire case, Akram did not provide any other reasons for why the prosecution did not want to proceed with trial for those four charges for now.
“There’s no stopping our power under Section 254(1) to apply, and nothing stops Your Ladyship’s power under Section 254(3) to grant full acquittal. We leave it to Your Ladyship’s discretion and wisdom to make the appropriate order,” he had said.
Akram also said the issue of freezing of Bersatu’s accounts is a separate matter filed in another court and is not relevant to the prosecution’s powers under Section 254(1) to discontinue the four charges.
Section 254(1) enables the prosecution to decide not to further prosecute an accused person at any stage of the trial (before judgment is delivered) and states that the accused will be discharged after the prosecution informs the court that it will not continue with the charges.
Section 254(3) states that an accused person’s discharge under Section 254(1) will not be an acquittal unless the court orders it.
In other words, Section 254(3) gives the court the power to decide to acquit an accused person, if the prosecution decides not to continue with the charges against the accused person.
After deliberating the arguments from both sides during lunch break, the judge decided to acquit Muhyiddin of the four charges.
Previously on August 19, the trial’s lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin had in court confirmed that Akram would be conducting the prosecution for the Bukhary Equity charges, and had confirmed business tycoon Tan Sri Syed Mokhtar Al-Bukhary was one of the witnesses to be called.
The prosecution had initially had a list of 18 prosecution witnesses for the charges involving Bukhary Equity funds.

Title: Ipsos poll: Malaysians prioritise jobs and homes over traditional milestones
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Malaysians largely mirror global views on success, prioritising stable employment and home ownership, yet they place a significantly higher premium on marriage and parenthood as life milestones, according to a new Ipsos report.
The Ipsos Life Aspirations 2026 report reveals that two in three Malaysians view stability and security as the primary markers of a successful life. Specifically, 67 per cent of Malaysians identify a stable job as essential, compared to 65 per cent globally, while 60 per cent view home ownership as a key milestone, slightly above the global average of 58 per cent.
The findings, based on a survey of 501 Malaysians aged 18 to 74, highlight a clear cultural emphasis on family.
Parenthood and marriage are viewed as markers of success by 47 per cent and 42 per cent of Malaysians, respectively, far outpacing global figures of 31 per cent and 25 per cent.
However, a generational divide is emerging. While the fundamentals of success remain broadly similar, Gen Z Malaysians are placing less emphasis on traditional family milestones than their Millennial counterparts.
Both generations agree on the primacy of career stability, with 69 per cent of Millennials and 68 per cent of Gen Z citing a full-time, stable job as the most important marker of success. Home ownership follows closely, cited by 64 per cent of Millennials and 55 per cent of Gen Z.
The gap in family aspirations is more pronounced: only 32 per cent of Gen Z respondents view marriage as a marker of success, compared to 58 per cent of Millennials. Similarly, only 35 per cent of Gen Z value parenthood as a milestone, against 50 per cent of Millennials.
Ipsos Malaysia managing director Arun Menon noted that this shift aligns with wider demographic trends, as Malaysians increasingly delay marriage and parenthood in favour of education, career progression, and financial security.
The most striking disparity, however, lies in home ownership. While 79 per cent of respondents aspire to own a home, only 46 per cent have achieved this goal, underscoring the persistent affordability crisis in the local housing market.
“Around three in four Malaysians aspire to own a home, yet fewer than half have achieved it, echoing the wider affordability challenges in Malaysia’s housing market,” Arun said.
He added that these findings suggest younger Malaysians are not necessarily redefining success, but are instead reordering their priorities, securing financial and personal stability before pursuing traditional life milestones.

Title: Muhyiddin trial: Lawyer accuses MACC officer of ‘intimidation’ over police report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 15 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad today told the High Court that a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer had allegedly attempted to intimidate and tarnish his reputation as a lawyer, based on the officer’s MACC colleague’s police report.
Amer, who was cross-examining MACC officer Mazery Mohd Zaini as the 29th prosecution witness yesterday in Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial, said the police report had false information.
Amer said the police report lodged yesterday had named him and referred to the ongoing trial, and referred to an alleged classified document that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had wanted to be included as evidence in the trial.
Amer said the MACC officer who lodged the police report had said he received information from the investigating officer in Muhyiddin’s trial, adding that he could only infer that it refers to Mazery who is still under oath and was scheduled to give evidence in court today.
“It’s clearly an attempt at intimidation,” he said. “But I’m not intimidated, they drew first blood and I will repay them with no quarters.”
Amer accused Mazery of trying to tarnish his reputation and trying to mislead the public via the police report’s claim that the document is not related to Muhyiddin’s trial, describing it as an “underhanded tactic” by a witness who was still testifying in court.
The alleged classified document was the statement that MACC had recorded from Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad during investigations.
“No court should condone this kind of tactic. Yang Arif is supposed to decide on subject matter of the case based on all facts and legal arguments. Yet the very IO whom we have challenged with several issues, decided to undermine the entire trial process by lodging this report,” he said.
Amer told the High Court that he is considering various legal action: “I will not exclude the possibility of lodging a report against the appropriate person including the IO for making false report, contempt of court and any other legal action. I reserve all those rights.”
“I’m making an application to this court to reserve my right to further cross this witness with regard to his underhanded tactic,” he added.
Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin is pictured at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex September 2, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik said the defence team stands in support of Amer, while fellow defence lawyer Datuk Seri K. Kumaraendran asked if the High Court would consider commencing contempt of court proceedings against Mazery.
Mazery then apologised to Amer and explained the police report made by his MACC colleague was only intended to ensure that there had been no leaks of classified information.
“First, I want to apologise to the lawyers, especially Datuk Amer, about the issue of report lodged. About that report, actually I worried that the document came from MACC officers, so I worried there is a leak of internal information from MACC officers. If there is, I have to protect my department, MACC’s integrity.
“That’s why the report was made to see if there was leaks from MACC itself. So we don’t want this classified document that is so important could simply go out, especially in the future,” he said, adding that he has no intention to hurt the image of the lawyers whom he had always respected.
Mazery said he may get the police report withdrawn if he finds there were no leaks by MACC officers.
After hearing Mazery’s explanation, Amer stressed that the document was provided by the prosecution to Adam Radlan’s lawyers in the latter’s own case, and that Muhyiddin’s lawyers had obtained the document from Adam Radlan’s lawyers.
“To clear the air, we obtained this document from the legal team representing Adam Radlan, we never obtained this document through any illegal or improper channels. So let it be clear, that the report has no basis whatsoever,” he said, adding that Mazery could have asked him first where the document came from instead of lodging the police report.
“I never obtained it from MACC, we never obtained it from MACC, 100 per cent,” Amer later said at another point, also adding that Muhyiddin’s lawyers are “entitled” to obtain it from Adam Radlan’s lawyers as they feel it is relevant to Muhyiddin’s trial.
While taking note of Mazery’s apology and explanation, Amer said he still reserves his rights and that his reputation remains tarnished for every second that the police report remains out there.
Amer had pointed out that the police report had been reported by the media.
After Muhyiddin’s lawyer Rosli Dahlan pressed for Mazery to inform the court that the police report would be withdrawn, the judge allowed Mazery’s request to carry out the necessary checks before withdrawing the report and also directed him to report to the court as soon as possible.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume this afternoon, with Mazery expected to update the court on the status of the police report.

Title: Police receive two reports over Negeri Sembilan MB’s alleged forced signing of royal document
Article:
SEREMBAN,  Sept 15 — Police have received two reports concerning the Proclamation document allegedly signed under duress by Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, seeking to remove the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said following the reports lodged by the Menteri Besar, the police would classify the case to determine the appropriate direction and scope of the investigation.
“I can confirm that two police reports were lodged by the Menteri Besar. It is our duty, upon receiving the reports, to classify them based on the nature and direction of the investigation.
“I leave it to the wisdom of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) to handle the complaint,” he told reporters here today.
He was met after presenting a sponsored Umrah package to Nurul Arini Abdullah, 19, who was among those assisted by the National Registration Department (JPN) in obtaining her identity card last year, and her mother, Norini Basir, 62, here today.
Saifuddin Nasution advised the public to respect the rule of law and refrain from making assumptions that could disrupt the investigation or public order.
Ismail had previously claimed that he was forced to sign the document before lodging a police report on Sept 8 to facilitate an investigation by the authorities.
Media reports previously quoted Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as saying that the allegation needed to be verified by the lawyer who was present during the signing process.
The UMNO president also said the party would not interfere in the matter, but fully respected the royal institution, laws and customs of Negeri Sembilan. — Bernama

Title: Pesta Pulau Pinang returns, but moves to Tasek Gelugor after 50 Years at Sungai Nibong
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 15 — Pesta Pulau Pinang will return this year for a month-long celebration starting December 1, with the event relocating to Padang Menora in Tasek Gelugor.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow confirmed that while the annual event continues as scheduled, it will be held at a more compact venue compared to its traditional site in Sungai Nibong.
“Although Padang Menora is smaller than the Sungai Nibong grounds, it is suitable for continuing the annual event,” Chow told reporters following the closing ceremony of the national-level Penang2030 public speaking competition at USM today.
The decision to move the event follows the closure of the original Pesta grounds to facilitate the construction of the Mutiara Line light rail transit (LRT) station and depot.
The state government had explored several alternative locations before the Penang Regional Development Authority (Perda) offered the Tasek Gelugor site.
Despite the change in venue, the state executive council decided to retain the name “Pesta Pulau Pinang,” acknowledging the brand’s prestige and recognition over the past half-century.
The event will run from December 1 to 31, with further details to be announced once finalised.
The former Pesta site in Sungai Nibong is now the focus of a proposed Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Masterplan covering approximately 23.47 hectares.
Developed through a collaboration between the state government, the Asian Development Bank, MRT Corporation, and various federal and state agencies, the draft master plan is expected to be finalised in October.
The vision for the site is to create a long-term, mixed-use transit hub integrating residential, commercial, and public facilities. This large-scale urban transformation is expected to take between 10 and 15 years to fully implement.
